column1: 51cefb12bc2986e7,"When the Regulator receives the relevant notice that would trigger informing Host Regulator(s) of an intent to use passporting procedures, in what circumstances must the Regulator refrain from sending that notice, and how does that affect the subsequent steps of publishing the Passported Fund’s details and notifying the Fund Manager once Host Regulator confirmation is received?","The Regulator’s obligation to notify Host Regulator(s) of its intent to use the passporting procedures is conditional: it must not send that notice if it considers the Fund Manager or the Private Fund is not compliant, or may become non-compliant, with applicable legislation (including these Rules), or if refraining is necessary and appropriate to advance one or more of the Regulator’s objectives. [#SRC:2f9bc2f5-72a6-45ee-8ec3-fac8a19ab60c] Where those conditions apply, the Regulator is required to refrain from transmitting the notice that would otherwise be sent within five Business Days of receiving the triggering notice, even though the general process contemplates providing that intent notice to the Host Regulator(s) in each relevant Host Jurisdiction where the Passported Fund is intended to be Promoted. [#TGT:49f2d65b-c143-456c-8e45-d05767ba59c7] Because the later steps are expressly tied to receiving confirmation from the Host Regulator(s) that their Register of Passported Funds has been updated, the Regulator would only proceed to (i) publish the Passported Fund’s details on the Register of Passported Funds and (ii) notify the Fund Manager that registration is complete after such Host Regulator confirmation occurs. [#TGT:49f2d65b-c143-456c-8e45-d05767ba59c7] In practical terms, if the Regulator must refrain from sending the intent notice due to the compliance/objectives grounds, the downstream publication and completion notification steps would not be reached through this pathway. [#SRC:2f9bc2f5-72a6-45ee-8ec3-fac8a19ab60c] [#TGT:49f2d65b-c143-456c-8e45-d05767ba59c7]","The Regulator shall not transmit a notice under Rule 3.1.4‎(a):

column2: if it considers that the Fund Manager or the Private Fund does not comply with, or it has reasonable grounds for determining that the Fund Manager or the Private Fund may in the future not comply with, applicable legislation including these Rules; or
if it considers that it is necessary and appropriate to refrain from doing so in order to further one or more of its objectives.","The Regulator shall:

Within five Business Days of receipt of the notice set out in Rule 3.1.2, and subject to Rule 3.1.5, provide notice of the intent to use the passporting procedures under these Rules to the Host Regulator(s) in the relevant Host Jurisdiction(s) where the Passported Fund is intended to be Promoted; and
promptly following confirmation from the relevant Host Regulator(s) that its respective Register of Passported Funds has been updated to include the details of the Passported Fund:
publish the details of the Passported Fund on the Register of Passported Funds; and

notify the Fund Manager that registration on the Register of Passported Funds is complete.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,2f9bc2f5-72a6-45ee-8ec3-fac8a19ab60c,49f2d65b-c143-456c-8e45-d05767ba59c7,,,3.1.5,3.1.4,,,,,HV0001,51cefb12bc2986e7,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 486dfdce3e64d73f,"When a Payment Order for an individual Payment Transaction is sent using a Payment Instrument issued under a Framework Contract, what information must the Payment Service Provider still provide immediately after initiation to the Payer (and where applicable the Payee), and what category of information may it omit because another Payment Service Provider has provided or will provide it under the Framework Contract?","For an individual Payment Transaction initiated by a Payment Order, the Payment Service Provider must, immediately after initiation, provide or make available specific transaction-level details to the Payer and, where applicable, to the Payee. [#SRC:a48a07c2-0731-4505-939e-07110e2af622] This includes confirmation that initiation with the Payer’s Payment Service Provider was successful, a reference that lets the Payer and Payee identify the Payment Transaction (including identifying the Payer and Payee and, where appropriate, information transferred with the Payment Order), the transaction amount in the currency used, any charges payable (and where applicable a breakdown in the Payment Order currency), exchange-rate information where currency conversion is used (including the actual rate or a reference to it and the post-conversion amount), the date the Payment Service Provider received the Payment Order, and the Credit Value Date. [#SRC:a48a07c2-0731-4505-939e-07110e2af622] However, where that Payment Order is transmitted via a Payment Instrument issued under a Framework Contract, the Payment Service Provider for that single Payment Transaction does not have to provide the general information that another Payment Service Provider has provided or will provide in relation to the Framework Contract. [#TGT:c337e2ea-0d58-45b9-970f-810639f88bf2]","Subject to Rule 19.5.3, a Payment Service Provider must provide or make available to the Payer and, where applicable, to the Payee, immediately after the initiation of a Payment Order:

column2: confirmation of the successful initiation of the Payment Order with the Payer’s Payment Service Provider;
a reference enabling the Payer and the Payee to identify the Payment Transaction, including the Payer and Payee, and, where appropriate, any information transferred with the Payment Order;
the amount of the Payment Transaction, in the currency used in the Payment Order;
the amount of any charges payable in relation to the Payment Transaction and, where applicable, a breakdown of the amounts of such charges expressed in the currency of the Payment Order;
where an exchange rate is used in the Payment Transaction the actual rate used or a reference to it, and the amount of the Payment Transaction after that currency conversion;
the date on which the Payment Service Provider received the Payment Order; and

the Credit Value Date.","Where a Payment Order for an individual Payment Transaction is transmitted by way of a Payment Instrument issued under a Framework Contract, the Payment Service Provider in respect of that single Payment Transaction need not provide or make available under Rule 19.5.1 the general information which has been provided or will be provided under Section 19.2 by another Payment Service Provider in respect of a Framework Contract.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,a48a07c2-0731-4505-939e-07110e2af622,c337e2ea-0d58-45b9-970f-810639f88bf2,,,19.5.1,19.5.3,,,,,HV0002,486dfdce3e64d73f,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 1171eaecafc1ce10,"When an Applicant/Authorised Person is pursuing a change such as migrating an MTF to become a conventional Securities Recognised Investment Exchange, and the Regulator expects substantial additional costs or effort in dealing with the related application or authorisation, what fee consequences can be imposed and what engagement is recommended?","If the circumstances create a substantial additional regulatory burden or substantial additional costs/effort for the Regulator in handling the matter, the Regulator can require payment of an extra fee on top of other fees. [#SRC:43df6a6a-29a3-4dca-8203-57b209ce85cc] [#TGT:64a0df5a-e946-4496-9fd3-244340c2a080] This can arise where the Regulator expects to incur substantial additional costs or expend substantial additional effort in dealing with an application, authorisation, filing, or during on-going supervision. [#TGT:64a0df5a-e946-4496-9fd3-244340c2a080] In the specific example of migrating an MTF to become a conventional Securities Recognised Investment Exchange, the FSRA indicates that such a scenario can be one where additional fees may be imposed because of the added regulatory burden. [#SRC:43df6a6a-29a3-4dca-8203-57b209ce85cc] In those circumstances, the FSRA recommends that the Applicant/Authorised Person proactively discuss the fee implications with the FSRA as early as practicable, rather than waiting until later in the process. [#SRC:43df6a6a-29a3-4dca-8203-57b209ce85cc]","FEES

Pursuant to FEES Rule 1.2.4, the FSRA reserves its right to impose additional fees in circumstances where a ‘substantial additional’ regulatory burden is imposed on FSRA. In such circumstances, including the migration of an MTF to become a conventional ‘Securities’ Recognised Investment Exchange, the FSRA recommends that the Applicant/Authorised Person discuss FEE implications with the FSRA as early as practicable.","Supplementary fees

The Regulator may require a Person to pay to the Regulator a supplementary fee in circumstances where it expects to incur substantial additional costs or expend substantial additional effort in dealing with an application, authorisation, filing or when conducting on-going supervision.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,43df6a6a-29a3-4dca-8203-57b209ce85cc,64a0df5a-e946-4496-9fd3-244340c2a080,,,187),1.2.4,,,,,HV0003,1171eaecafc1ce10,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

899e964325c9691b,"For a Customer that is not a Natural Person, if the Customer and the Third Party Provider have agreed in writing to change the time period for notifying unauthorised or incorrectly executed Payment Transactions, how does that interact with the Customer’s entitlement to redress when the Third Party Provider did not provide or make available information about the Third Party Transaction as required?","If the Customer is not a Natural Person, the Customer and the Third Party Provider can, by written agreement, set a different notification time period for unauthorised or incorrectly executed Payment Transactions for the purposes of the notification time period that would otherwise apply. [#SRC:10510c2c-99d3-4cba-bac5-61cda5d00d44] Separately, where the Third Party Provider has not provided or made available information about the Third Party Transaction in the required manner, the Customer remains entitled to redress even if the Customer did not notify the Third Party Provider within the notification time period that would otherwise be applicable. [#TGT:e0ee4cf0-d2ae-4d3b-8012-62c5be6043a7] Taken together, this means that a written agreement changing the notification time period does not remove the Customer’s ability to obtain redress in the specific circumstance where the Third Party Provider’s failure relates to providing or making available the required transaction information. [#SRC:10510c2c-99d3-4cba-bac5-61cda5d00d44] [#TGT:e0ee4cf0-d2ae-4d3b-8012-62c5be6043a7] In practice, the Customer’s entitlement to redress in that information-failure scenario applies even if the Customer misses the otherwise-applicable notification deadline, including where that deadline has been altered by written agreement for this type of Customer. [#SRC:10510c2c-99d3-4cba-bac5-61cda5d00d44] [#TGT:e0ee4cf0-d2ae-4d3b-8012-62c5be6043a7]","Where the Customer is not a Natural Person, the Customer and the Third Party Provider may agree in writing that the following Rules do not apply:

column2: Rules 20.2.15 and 20.2.16 (charges for information);
Rule 20.7.3 and 20.7.4 (withdrawal of consent);
Rule 20.8.2 (revocation of a Payment Order);
Rules 20.10.1 and 20.10.2 (requests for refund);
Rule 20.11.1 (evidence on authentication and execution);
Rule 20.12.5 (liability for charges); and

column1: the parties may agree that a different time period applies concerning unauthorised or incorrectly executed Payment Transactions for the purposes of Rule 20.10.1.","Where the Third Party Provider has failed to provide or make available information concerning the Third Party Transaction in accordance with Section 20.3, the Customer is entitled to redress even if the Customer has failed to notify the Third Party Provider within the time period set out in Rule 20.10.1.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,10510c2c-99d3-4cba-bac5-61cda5d00d44,e0ee4cf0-d2ae-4d3b-8012-62c5be6043a7,,,20.4.1,20.10.2,,,,,HV0004,899e964325c9691b,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

9d433957cee557b9,"When an Authorised Person wants to treat Exposures as collateralised using cash received under a CLN it issued, or using loans and Deposits of a Counterparty that are subject to an on balance sheet Netting agreement, what conditions must be satisfied before the Authorised Person can recognise the effects of CRM for that Collateral?","An Authorised Person may treat Exposures as collateralised only if the relevant CRM conditions are met, including where the collateral consists of cash received under a CLN issued by the Authorised Person or loans and Deposits of a Counterparty to or with the Authorised Person that are subject to an on balance sheet Netting agreement recognised for CRM purposes. [#SRC:558596ee-af40-4c07-8067-9c5c25eebaa5] Before recognising the effects of CRM of any such Collateral, the Authorised Person must ensure specific recognition requirements are satisfied. [#TGT:cb37e5c4-ed71-4523-8fb8-da4fbc7eecf1] These include having a legal mechanism that gives the Authorised Person timely rights to liquidate or take legal possession upon the Counterparty’s default/insolvency (and, if applicable, the custodian’s credit event), and taking all steps needed under applicable law to obtain and maintain an enforceable security interest (including registration where relevant) or to exercise netting/set-off rights for title transfer collateral. [#TGT:cb37e5c4-ed71-4523-8fb8-da4fbc7eecf1] The Authorised Person must also ensure there is no material positive correlation between Counterparty credit quality and Collateral value, exclude Securities issued by the Counterparty or any Closely Related Counterparty, implement procedures for timely liquidation that observe legal default conditions, and—if a custodian holds the Collateral—take reasonable steps to ensure segregation from the custodian’s own assets. [#TGT:cb37e5c4-ed71-4523-8fb8-da4fbc7eecf1]",An Authorised Person can only treat Exposures as collateralised provided the conditions of Rules 4.13.5 to 4.13.8 (relating to CRM) are met. Item (d) also includes cash received under a CLN issued by the Authorised Person and loans and Deposits of a Counterparty to or with the Authorised Person which are subject to an on balance sheet Netting agreement recognised under Section 4.13 (CRM).,"Requirements for Recognition of Collateral. An Authorised Person must ensure that the following requirements are complied with before it recognises the effects of CRM of any Collateral:

column2: the legal mechanism by which Collateral is pledged, assigned or transferred must confer on the Authorised Person the right to liquidate or take legal possession of the Collateral, in a timely manner, in the event of the default, insolvency or bankruptcy (or one or more otherwise defined credit events set out in the transaction documentation) of the Counterparty (and, where applicable, of the custodian holding the Collateral);

the Authorised Person has taken all steps necessary to fulfil those requirements under the law applicable to the Authorised Person's interest in the Collateral for obtaining and maintaining an enforceable security interest by registering it with a registrar or for exercising a right to net or set off in relation to title transfer Collateral;
the credit quality of the Counterparty and the value of the Collateral do not have a material positive correlation;
Securities issued by the Counterparty or any Closely Related Counterparty are not eligible;

the Authorised Person has implemented procedures for the timely liquidation of Collateral to ensure that any legal conditions required for declaring default of Counterparty and liquidating the Collateral are observed, and that the Collateral can be liquidated promptly; and

where the Collateral is held by a custodian, the Authorised Person has taken reasonable steps to ensure that the custodian segregates the Collateral from its own assets.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,558596ee-af40-4c07-8067-9c5c25eebaa5,cb37e5c4-ed71-4523-8fb8-da4fbc7eecf1,,,APP4.A4.11.1.Guidance.2.,4.13.8,,,,,HV0005,9d433957cee557b9,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 8c6e94dd4640227e,"When an Authorised Person is considering a guarantee as credit risk mitigation for a credit risk exposure to a multilateral development bank, what conditions must be met for the guarantee to be eligible for recognition, and what risk weight must be applied to the exposure if the MDB is one of the qualifying institutions listed (for example, IBRD/IFC/MIGA within the World Bank Group)?","For a guarantee to be recognised as credit risk mitigation, the Authorised Person may only recognise its effects if the guarantor is within the permitted set of entities (including a central government or central bank, a PSE, qualifying banks and Securities firms, or another entity with an external credit assessment from a recognised credit rating agency mapping to Credit Quality Grade 3 or better). [#SRC:281505d3-a15a-449a-9095-dc247d0e2e5d] Separately, where the credit risk exposure is to a qualifying multilateral development bank in the specified list, the Authorised Person must apply a 0% risk weight to that credit risk exposure. [#TGT:aed2a764-3ad1-4646-bf24-f6416556ffb4] This means that, in the scenario described, the compliance analysis has two linked steps: first confirm the guarantor meets one of the eligibility categories for recognising the guarantee’s CRM effect; then, if the exposure is to a listed qualifying MDB (such as the World Bank Group entities IBRD, MIGA, and IFC), apply the mandated 0% risk weight to the exposure. [#SRC:281505d3-a15a-449a-9095-dc247d0e2e5d] [#TGT:aed2a764-3ad1-4646-bf24-f6416556ffb4]","An Authorised Person may recognise the effects of CRM of a guarantee only if it is provided by any of the following entities:

column2: central government or central bank;
MDB referred to in Rule 4.12.8;
International Organisations referred to in Rule 4.12.9;
PSE;
banks and Securities firms which qualify for inclusion in bank asset class; or

any other entity that has an external credit assessment from a recognised credit rating agency that maps to a Credit Quality Grade 3 or better.","Multilateral development bank (MDB) asset class. An Authorised Person must apply a 0% risk weight to any CR Exposure to the qualifying MDBs set out below:

The World Bank Group comprised of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), and the International Finance Corporation (IFC);
The Asian Development Bank (ADB);
The African Development Bank (AfDB);
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD);
The Inter American Development Bank (IADB);
The European Investment Bank (EIB);
The European Investment Fund (EIF);
The Nordic Investment Bank (NIB);
The Caribbean Development Bank (CDB);
The Islamic Development Bank (IDB); and

The Council of Europe Development Bank (CEDB).",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,281505d3-a15a-449a-9095-dc247d0e2e5d,aed2a764-3ad1-4646-bf24-f6416556ffb4,,,4.13.9.(1),4.12.8,,,,,HV0006,8c6e94dd4640227e,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 82d2843886eaf674,"When an annual designation fee is due partway through a calendar year, how should the payable amount be calculated and by when must the initial annual fee be paid to the Regulator?","If the annual designation fee becomes due during the calendar year, the amount payable is not the full-year amount; it is a portion calculated by reference to how many months remain until the end of that calendar year. [#SRC:94b3f85d-c033-41a3-a884-c873899c049f] In that same situation, the initial annual fee must still be paid in full (as calculated on that prorated basis) to the Regulator within twenty days from the date the fee becomes due. [#TGT:b8f50488-8fd2-4f32-a6c6-d841b3c60c37] Practically, this means you first determine the prorated portion by counting the months remaining to year-end, and then you ensure the resulting prorated amount is remitted to the Regulator no later than the twentieth day after the due date. [#SRC:94b3f85d-c033-41a3-a884-c873899c049f] [#TGT:b8f50488-8fd2-4f32-a6c6-d841b3c60c37] This timing-and-calculation approach applies specifically to the initial annual fee that is prorated for the remainder of the calendar year, distinguishing it from later annual fees that relate to a period commencing on 1 January. [#TGT:b8f50488-8fd2-4f32-a6c6-d841b3c60c37]","In accordance with Rule 1.2.2, for Rule 10.2.1(a) the portion due of the annual designation fee is to be based on the number of months remaining until the end of the calendar year.","In regard to fees payable on an annual basis pursuant to these Rules:

column2: the initial annual fee must be paid in full to the Regulator within twenty days of the date on which the fee becomes due, prorated for the remainder of the calendar year; and

subsequent annual fees for the period commencing 1 January are payable in advance and must be paid in full to the Regulator on or before 31 January of the calendar year to which the fee relates.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,94b3f85d-c033-41a3-a884-c873899c049f,b8f50488-8fd2-4f32-a6c6-d841b3c60c37,,,10.2.1.Guidance,1.2.2,,,,,HV0007,82d2843886eaf674,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 536f2d2c37481d91,"When a PFP Operator publishes information for a PFP Prospect and later there is a material change, what must the PFP Operator do to update that published information and notify PFP Clients, and how does that interact with the PFP Operator’s record-keeping duties for disclosures and related transaction documentation?","A PFP Operator must treat a material change as triggering both an updating/notification obligation and a related retention obligation. Specifically, the PFP Operator must update the information it has published so that it reflects the material change, and it must also give PFP Clients notice of that material change within a reasonable timeframe after the change occurs. [#TGT:40149b11-dcb8-48a6-ab09-8d8c37923183] In parallel, the PFP Operator must maintain and keep records for at least six years that include all disclosures made under the same disclosure framework used for the published information, as well as all documentation exchanged between PFP Client(s), any Body Corporate established by the PFP Operator to facilitate a transaction, and the PFP Prospect. [#SRC:94d5a3fb-7438-42dd-8c48-70588f3d0dd7] This means that, when the published information is updated and clients are notified, the operator should ensure those disclosure-related materials and the associated communications/documentation connected to the PFP Prospect are retained for the minimum six-year period. [#SRC:94d5a3fb-7438-42dd-8c48-70588f3d0dd7] The retention duty also extends to keeping a record of the due diligence undertaken under the applicable due diligence requirement. [#SRC:94d5a3fb-7438-42dd-8c48-70588f3d0dd7]","A PFP Operator must, for a minimum of six years, maintain and keep a record of:

column2: all disclosures made in accordance with Rules 18.5.1 and 18.5.2;
all documentation between PFP Client(s), any Body Corporate established by the PFP Operator to facilitate a transaction, and the PFP Prospect; and

the due diligence undertaken in accordance with Rule 18.4.1.",A PFP Operator must ensure that the information published in accordance with Rule 18.5.1 is updated to reflect material changes and notice of such material change is provided to PFP Clients within a reasonable timeframe following such change.,DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,94d5a3fb-7438-42dd-8c48-70588f3d0dd7,40149b11-dcb8-48a6-ab09-8d8c37923183,,,18.7.1,18.5.2,,,,,HV0008,536f2d2c37481d91,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 85c7a88a32028ce9,"How should an Authorised Person determine whether it falls within Category 2 or Category 3A when its Financial Services Permission includes Dealing in Investments as Principal and/or Dealing in Investments as Agent, including the case where principal dealing is only as a Matched Principal and the case where agent dealing is wholly incidental to Managing an Investment Fund or Managing Assets?","To classify the Authorised Person, first distinguish whether any permission to deal as principal is unrestricted or limited to matched-principal dealing, and then confirm whether any exclusion from other categories applies. If the Financial Services Permission authorises Providing Credit or Dealing in Investments as Principal other than as Matched Principal, and the dealing activities are not limited in scope as described, the Authorised Person is treated as Category 2 provided it also does not meet the criteria of Categories 1 or 5. [#SRC:6737c8c3-06cb-4da7-bbcd-9e8650ecf66f] In contrast, Category 3A applies where the permission covers Dealing in Investments as Principal only as a Matched Principal and/or Dealing in Investments as Agent, and the Authorised Person does not meet the criteria of Categories 1, 2 or 5. [#TGT:458af530-cdd6-42ca-a3ca-ef81822f63df] As an explicit linkage, even if the Authorised Person has permission for Dealing in Investments as Agent (a Category 3A-type activity), where it carries out that agent dealing wholly incidentally to Managing an Investment Fund or Managing Assets, it is regarded as falling within Category 3C rather than being treated solely by reference to the Category 3A permission description. [#SRC:6737c8c3-06cb-4da7-bbcd-9e8650ecf66f] Accordingly, matched-principal-only dealing supports Category 3A unless Category 3C treatment applies due to wholly incidental agent dealing, while non-matched-principal dealing supports Category 2 if the other stated conditions are met. [#SRC:6737c8c3-06cb-4da7-bbcd-9e8650ecf66f] [#TGT:458af530-cdd6-42ca-a3ca-ef81822f63df]","An Authorised Person is in Category 2 if:

column2: its Financial Services Permission authorises it to carry on one or both of the Regulated Activities of Providing Credit or Dealing in Investments as Principal (not as Matched Principal);
its dealing activities are not limited in scope as provided in Rule 1.3.3(1)(a)(i); and
it does not meet the criteria of Categories 1 or 5.

column1: A Category 3A Authorised Person may be authorised to conduct other Regulated Activities, but it is the authorisation for Dealing in Investments as Agent and the absence of authorisation for the activities specified in Rules 1.3.1 and 1.3.2 that are determinative of its belonging to Category 3A. Provided that an Authorised Person carries out the Regulated Activity of Dealing in Investments as Agent in a manner that is wholly incidental to the activity of Managing an Investment Fund or Managing Assets, the Authorised Person shall be regarded as falling within Category 3C.","An Authorised Person is in Category 3A if:

column2: its Financial Services Permission authorises it to carry on one or more of the Regulated Activities of:
Dealing in Investments as Principal (where it does so only as a Matched Principal); or
Dealing in Investments as Agent; and

it does not meet the criteria of Categories 1, 2 or 5.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,6737c8c3-06cb-4da7-bbcd-9e8650ecf66f,458af530-cdd6-42ca-a3ca-ef81822f63df,,,1.3.2,1.3.3.(1),,,,,HV0009,85c7a88a32028ce9,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 40f73736e9dd62ec,"When a Recognised Investment Exchange uses a Price Reporting Agency for establishing prices of a Financial Instrument, what ongoing review arrangements must the Recognised Investment Exchange maintain, and what specific operational and governance features must the Price Reporting Agency continue to satisfy for that review to be meaningful?","A Recognised Investment Exchange must maintain arrangements that periodically reassess whether the Price Reporting Agency still satisfies the applicable requirements, rather than treating the agency’s status as a one-time determination. [#SRC:7728ff1d-b279-4806-b3fd-13f3e8a34e79] To make that ongoing review meaningful, the Recognised Investment Exchange’s review should be capable of checking that the Price Reporting Agency continues to meet the required features, including: having public, fair, and non-discriminatory procedures for establishing prices of a Financial Instrument; providing sufficient transparency about methodology, calculations, and inputs so users can understand how a benchmark or index is derived and its limitations; and, where appropriate, prioritising concluded transactions while taking measures to reduce selective reporting. [#TGT:8a81e6cb-f1f1-4988-af97-f966f288017a] The review should also cover whether the agency remains independent and reputable, maintains a sound corporate governance framework, has arrangements to prevent staff conflicts of interest that could materially harm the price establishment process, and operates adequate mechanisms to resolve complaints about its assessment process and methodology. [#TGT:8a81e6cb-f1f1-4988-af97-f966f288017a] In practice, the Recognised Investment Exchange’s arrangements must be set up to revisit these criteria regularly to confirm continued compliance over time. [#SRC:7728ff1d-b279-4806-b3fd-13f3e8a34e79]",A Recognised Investment Exchange must have arrangements in place to regularly review whether a Price Reporting Agency continues to meet the requirements of Rule 3.11.2.,"For the purposes of Rules 3.11.1 and 3.11.3, a Price Reporting Agency must:

column2: have fair and non-discriminatory procedures for establishing prices of a Financial Instrument, which are made public;
demonstrate adequate and appropriate transparency over the methodology, calculation and inputs to allow users to understand how the benchmark or index is derived and its potential limitations;
where appropriate, give priority to concluded transactions in making assessments and adopt measures to minimise selective reporting;
be of good standing and repute as an independent and objective price reporting agency or index provider;
have a sound corporate governance framework;
have adequate arrangements to avoid its staff having any conflicts of interest where such conflicts are, or are likely to have, a material adverse impact on a price establishment process; and

adequate complaint resolution mechanisms to resolve any complaints about its assessment process and methodology.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,7728ff1d-b279-4806-b3fd-13f3e8a34e79,8a81e6cb-f1f1-4988-af97-f966f288017a,,,3.11.3,3.11.2,,,,,HV0010,40f73736e9dd62ec,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 6697fc0bf46b866e,How should an Authorised Person calculate the annual supervision fees payable to the Regulator when it both (i) operates as a Cell Company with multiple Cells and (ii) holds a Financial Services Permission to carry on Effecting Contracts of Insurance and/or Carrying Out Contracts of Insurance as a Captive Insurer or an Insurance Special Purpose Vehicle?,"An Authorised Person in this combined situation must treat the annual supervision fee as the sum of two distinct fee components that apply on different bases: one tied to operating as a Cell Company (including a per-Cell amount) and another tied to carrying on specified insurance activities as a Captive Insurer or an Insurance Special Purpose Vehicle. [#SRC:3256d044-7e1a-46ff-82d5-db50175eae7b] [#TGT:9240b52a-9167-41c8-a2aa-aba636e47579] First, if the Authorised Person operates as a Cell Company, it must pay an additional annual supervision fee of $8,000 for the Cell Company itself, plus $1,000 for each Cell it has. [#SRC:3256d044-7e1a-46ff-82d5-db50175eae7b] Second, if the Authorised Person has a Financial Services Permission to carry on either one or both of the Regulated Activities of Effecting Contracts of Insurance or Carrying Out Contracts of Insurance as a Captive Insurer or an Insurance Special Purpose Vehicle, it must pay an annual supervision fee of $5,000 covering either or both of those Regulated Activities. [#TGT:9240b52a-9167-41c8-a2aa-aba636e47579] Accordingly, the total annual supervision fees payable to the Regulator are calculated by adding the Cell Company amount ($8,000 + $1,000 per Cell) to the $5,000 amount applicable to the permitted captive/insurance special purpose vehicle activities. [#SRC:3256d044-7e1a-46ff-82d5-db50175eae7b] [#TGT:9240b52a-9167-41c8-a2aa-aba636e47579]","Cell Companies. An Authorised Person under Rule 3.11.2 or Rule 3.11.4 that operates as a Cell Company must pay to the Regulator an additional annual supervision fee of $8,000 for the Cell Company plus $1,000 for each Cell.","Captive Insurers and Insurance Special Purpose Vehicles. An Authorised Person with a Financial Services Permission to carry on either one or both of the Regulated Activities of Effecting Contracts of Insurance or Carrying Out Contracts of Insurance as a Captive Insurer or an Insurance Special Purpose Vehicle must pay to the Regulator an annual supervision fee of $5,000 for either or both Regulated Activities.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,3256d044-7e1a-46ff-82d5-db50175eae7b,9240b52a-9167-41c8-a2aa-aba636e47579,,,3.11.6,3.11.4,,,,,HV0011,6697fc0bf46b866e,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

88b9c6fa0ca55fb3,"If an Originator provides non-contractual support to a securitisation transaction in order to reduce investors’ potential or actual losses beyond what the transaction documents require, what compliance consequences and investor-facing disclosures apply, including how the Originator must treat the underlying Exposures and any gain on sale?","Providing non-contractual support to a securitisation transaction to reduce investors’ potential or actual losses beyond contractual obligations is prohibited conduct for an Originator (and also for a Sponsor). [#TGT:a7d00358-0608-4ba6-b012-36de1be9cc2f] Where the Originator nonetheless fails to comply with the relevant requirement in respect of the securitisation, the Originator must apply specific prudential and disclosure consequences tied to that implicit support. [#SRC:5443b1af-d668-49ad-8014-990d90fcba1c] In particular, the Originator must (i) include all underlying Exposures of the securitisation in its Credit RWA calculation as though the Exposures had not been securitised and remained on the balance sheet of the Authorised Person, (ii) refrain from recognising any gain on sale of assets to the securitisation, and (iii) disclose to investors both that the Authorised Person has provided non-contractual support and the regulatory capital impact of doing so. [#SRC:5443b1af-d668-49ad-8014-990d90fcba1c] These consequences operationalise the prohibition by removing capital and accounting benefits and ensuring investors are informed when implicit (non-contractual) support has been provided. [#TGT:a7d00358-0608-4ba6-b012-36de1be9cc2f]","Implicit Support. If an Originator fails to comply with Rule 4.14.15 in respect of a securitisation, it:

column2: must include all the underlying Exposures of the securitisation in its calculation of Credit RWAs as if those Exposures had not been securitised and were on the balance sheet of the Authorised Person;
must not recognise any gain on sale of assets to the securitisation; and

must disclose to investors that the Authorised Person has provided non-contractual support and the regulatory capital impact of doing so.",Implicit Support. An Originator or a Sponsor of a securitisation must not provide Implicit Support to a securitisation transaction with a view to reducing potential or actual losses to investors outside of its contractual obligations;,DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,5443b1af-d668-49ad-8014-990d90fcba1c,a7d00358-0608-4ba6-b012-36de1be9cc2f,,,4.14.16,4.14.15,,,,,HV0012,88b9c6fa0ca55fb3,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: daa28727b917ba23,"If the Fund Manager identifies a material change, error, or omission after making the cross-border notification but before Promotion starts in a Host Jurisdiction, what notifications must be made and what regulatory measures may follow if that issue means the Fund Manager would no longer comply with applicable legislation (including these Rules) or the Regulator considers action necessary?","Between the cross-border notification and the start of Promotion in a Host Jurisdiction, once the Fund Manager becomes aware of a material change, error, or omission that is reasonably likely to matter to that notification, the Fund Manager must notify the Regulator in writing without delay. [#TGT:b27b7465-dcf2-43cf-a342-6f999ce5dadc] After receiving that notice, the Regulator is expected to promptly pass all relevant details of the material change, error, or omission to the relevant Host Regulator. [#TGT:b27b7465-dcf2-43cf-a342-6f999ce5dadc] In addition to this notification-and-forwarding process, if the material change, error, or omission results in the Fund Manager no longer complying with applicable legislation (including these Rules), or if the Regulator otherwise considers it necessary in the circumstances, the Regulator must take all due measures. [#SRC:9845037b-efae-4710-b7ca-81473eac1aee] Those measures can include, where necessary, de-registering the Public Fund from the Register of Passported Funds in accordance with these Rules. [#SRC:9845037b-efae-4710-b7ca-81473eac1aee] Accordingly, the Fund Manager’s immediate written notice during the pre-Promotion window can trigger both onward communication to the Host Regulator and potential escalated action up to de-registration if compliance is jeopardized or the Regulator deems it necessary. [#SRC:9845037b-efae-4710-b7ca-81473eac1aee] [#TGT:b27b7465-dcf2-43cf-a342-6f999ce5dadc]","If, as a result of any material change, error, or omission referred to in Rule 3.2.9, the Fund Manager will no longer comply with applicable legislation, including these Rules, or if the Regulator otherwise considers it necessary in the circumstances, the Regulator shall take all due measures, including, if necessary, the de-registration of the Public Fund from the Register of Passported Funds in accordance with these Rules.","If, at any time between the notification pursuant to Rule 3.2.2 and the commencement of Promotion in a Host Jurisdiction, the Fund Manager becomes aware of any material change, error, or omission reasonably likely to be relevant to such notification, the Fund Manager shall give written notice to the Regulator without delay.  The Regulator will promptly provide the relevant Host Regulator with all relevant details of the material change, error or omission.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,9845037b-efae-4710-b7ca-81473eac1aee,b27b7465-dcf2-43cf-a342-6f999ce5dadc,,,3.2.10,3.2.9,,,,,HV0013,daa28727b917ba23,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

254547bc372b5cb1,"When designing the strategy’s system for controlling Liquidity Risk, what capabilities and governance features must it include so that the Authorised Person can both implement the Liquidity Risk requirements and allow the Governing Body and senior management to oversee compliance with limits and operating procedures?","The strategy’s system for controlling Liquidity Risk must be constructed so it both supports implementation of the Liquidity Risk requirements and embeds governance oversight and control features within the Authorised Person’s Liquidity Risk framework. [#TGT:5c690bca-7ecd-4950-8e21-6c4cb9357647] In particular, the Authorised Person must ensure the system enables the Authorised Person’s Governing Body and senior management to review whether the Authorised Person is complying with the relevant limits and operating procedures, including limits set in accordance with the specified limits-setting requirement. [#SRC:844184dc-c876-465f-8cc6-61d7c4911988] The system must also include appropriate approval processes, limits, and other mechanisms that are designed to provide reasonable assurance that the Authorised Person’s Liquidity Risk management processes are followed in practice. [#SRC:844184dc-c876-465f-8cc6-61d7c4911988] Read together, this means the “system for controlling Liquidity Risk” that the strategy must include is not merely descriptive; it must be operationally capable of implementing the Liquidity Risk requirements while also providing structured oversight by the Governing Body and senior management and embedding approvals and control mechanisms to drive adherence to the Liquidity Risk management processes. [#TGT:5c690bca-7ecd-4950-8e21-6c4cb9357647] [#SRC:844184dc-c876-465f-8cc6-61d7c4911988]","Controlling Liquidity Risk. An Authorised Person must ensure that the system referred to in Rule 9.2.1(5):

column2: enables the Authorised Person's Governing Body and senior management to review compliance with limits set in accordance with Rule 9.2.7 and operating procedures; and

has appropriate approval processes, limits and other mechanisms designed to provide reasonable assurance that the Authorised Person's Liquidity Risk management processes are adhered to.",The strategy must include a system for controlling Liquidity Risk which enables the Authorised Person to implement the requirements set out in Rule 9.2.6.,DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,844184dc-c876-465f-8cc6-61d7c4911988,5c690bca-7ecd-4950-8e21-6c4cb9357647,,,9.2.6,9.2.1.(5),,,,,HV0014,254547bc372b5cb1,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,source_only_sufficient,

column1: 355cf8097915d2c8,"Before an Authorised Person offers OTC Leveraged Products to a Retail Client (or advises or makes arrangements for them), what assessment must be completed and what risk-understanding conclusion must be reached, given the expectation that the Authorised Person considers the Retail Client’s understanding of risks and the potential magnitude of losses before establishing a business relationship?","Before offering OTC Leveraged Products to a Retail Client—or providing advice or making arrangements on the Retail Client’s behalf relating to those products—the Authorised Person must first complete an assessment that covers the Retail Client’s skill, experience, knowledge, financial resources, and risk tolerance. [#TGT:be7639eb-37d0-4a64-80e4-a7694dd68cc0] This product-related assessment must be completed in a way that allows the Authorised Person to reasonably conclude two outcomes: first, that the Retail Client has adequate experience and skill to understand the potential risk of loss involved in investing in OTC Leveraged Products; and second, that the Retail Client has liquid financial resources sufficient to absorb potential losses from trading in OTC Leveraged Products. [#TGT:be7639eb-37d0-4a64-80e4-a7694dd68cc0] In addition, before establishing a business relationship with a Retail Client, the Authorised Person is expected to consider whether the Retail Client demonstrates an understanding of the risks and the potential magnitude of losses to which they may be exposed. [#SRC:e79e3adf-b4c6-4c32-81c3-6440c56574a6] Practically, this means the pre-relationship consideration of risk and loss magnitude should align with, and be evidenced through, the OTC Leveraged Products assessment and its required reasonable conclusions on loss-risk understanding and loss-absorption capacity. [#SRC:e79e3adf-b4c6-4c32-81c3-6440c56574a6] [#TGT:be7639eb-37d0-4a64-80e4-a7694dd68cc0]","In order to satisfy the requirements imposed by Rule 23.5.1, the Authorised Person should, prior to establishing a business relationship with a Retail Client, consider whether such Retail Client demonstrates an understanding of the risks and potential magnitude of losses which they may be exposed to.","An Authorised Person must not offer OTC Leveraged Products to a Retail Client, or provide any advice or make arrangements on behalf of a Retail Client relating to OTC Leveraged Products unless it has first completed an assessment of the skill, experience, knowledge, financial resources and risk tolerance of the Retail Client, such that the Authorised Person may reasonably conclude that the Retail Client has:

column2: adequate experience and skill enabling them to understand the potential risk of loss involved in investing in OTC Leveraged Products; and

liquid financial resources sufficient to absorb potential losses resulting from trading in OTC Leveraged Products.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,e79e3adf-b4c6-4c32-81c3-6440c56574a6,be7639eb-37d0-4a64-80e4-a7694dd68cc0,,,23.5.1.Guidance.1.,23.5.1,,,,,HV0015,355cf8097915d2c8,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 3e4ce8a5e87a8dc8,"For an Authorised Person that is a Domestic Firm and has been given an Individual Capital Requirement (ICR) arising from Pillar 2 adjustments, what capital resources must it maintain at all times, and how does that ICR-related obligation interact with the broader expectation to hold capital and liquid assets adequate to its business profile so liabilities can be met when due?","An Authorised Person that is a Domestic Firm and has an ICR must continuously meet two layers of capital-related expectations: (i) the baseline requirement to maintain Capital Resources calculated under the Rules, and (ii) an additional, ICR-specific requirement to hold extra Capital Resources of the specified type and amount. [#TGT:afbb9f59-2c26-47f6-ac38-4c36ecd40d56] [#SRC:776c1fbb-de2a-4be6-b5fe-7b1666b6abff] In practice, this means the firm must, at all times, have and maintain Capital Resources of the types and amounts required by the Rules and calculated in accordance with them. [#TGT:afbb9f59-2c26-47f6-ac38-4c36ecd40d56] If the Regulator has imposed an ICR due to Pillar 2 adjustments, the firm must also maintain, at all times, adequate Capital Resources of the type and amount specified for that ICR, on top of the Capital Resources it keeps to meet its capital adequacy requirements. [#SRC:776c1fbb-de2a-4be6-b5fe-7b1666b6abff] Alongside these capital-resource calculations and any ICR add-on, the Domestic Firm must also ensure it holds capital and liquid assets that are adequate for the nature, size, and complexity of its business so there is no significant risk it cannot meet liabilities as they fall due. [#TGT:afbb9f59-2c26-47f6-ac38-4c36ecd40d56]","Capital ratios. The Regulator may impose a further requirement, termed an Individual Capital Requirement (ICR), on an Authorised Person to hold additional Capital Resources arising from Pillar 2 adjustments (see Chapter 10).  Where the Authorised Person has an ICR imposed on it, then the Authorised Person must, at all times, maintain adequate Capital Resources of the type and amount as specified in Rule 10.6.1 in addition to those kept to meet the capital adequacy requirements outlined in Rule 3.2.4.","Domestic Firms – maintaining capital resources. An Authorised Person that is a Domestic Firm must:

column2: have and maintain, at all times, Capital Resources of the types and amounts specified in, and calculated in accordance with, these Rules;

ensure that it maintains capital and liquid assets in addition to the requirement in (a) which are adequate in relation to the nature, size and complexity of its business to ensure that there is no significant risk that liabilities cannot be met as they fall due.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,776c1fbb-de2a-4be6-b5fe-7b1666b6abff,afbb9f59-2c26-47f6-ac38-4c36ecd40d56,,,3.16.3,3.2.4,,,,,HV0016,3e4ce8a5e87a8dc8,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: e734025e4ea2af5a,"When an Investigator needs help to advance an investigation—such as locating particular documents—what forms of assistance can the Investigator compel, and what procedural mechanism and scope of persons can be used to impose that requirement?","An Investigator can compel assistance that advances an investigation, including requiring a person to carry out a physical act or to provide information, and this can extend to help with locating specific documents. [#SRC:c595f91e-fb49-45e1-9dd6-7a847f54df95] To impose these requirements, the Investigator may use a written notice directed either to the Person Under Investigation or to any other person, even if that other person is not connected to the Person Under Investigation. [#TGT:ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046] The written notice can require the recipient to provide assistance as the Investigator requires, which operationalizes the broader concept of compelled assistance (including physical acts and information provision) described for advancing the investigation. [#TGT:ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046] [#SRC:c595f91e-fb49-45e1-9dd6-7a847f54df95] In the same notice, the Investigator may also require related cooperation steps that can support document-location efforts, such as attending an interview at a specified time and place to answer questions, producing specified documents (or documents of a specified description) at a specified time and place, providing information the Investigator requires, or permitting entry to business premises during normal business hours to inspect and copy documents. [#TGT:ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046]","Power to require assistance. Section 206(1)(d) of FSMR empowers the Investigator to require a person to provide assistance in relation to an investigation, which may include requiring a person to do a physical act or provide information to advance an investigation. For example, an Investigator may require a person to assist in the location of specific documents.","The Investigator may, by written notice, require the person who is the Person Under Investigation or any other person (whether or not connected to the Person Under Investigation) to—

column2: attend an interview at a Specified time and place and answer questions;
produce at a Specified time and place any Specified Documents or Documents of a Specified description;
provide such information as the Investigator may require;
provide such assistance as the Investigator may require; or

permit the Investigator to enter the business premises of such person during normal business hours for the purpose of inspecting and copying Documents on such premises.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,c595f91e-fb49-45e1-9dd6-7a847f54df95,ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046,,,6.6.14,Part 17.206.(1),,,,,HV0017,e734025e4ea2af5a,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 15e360fdadbfb19a,"When a Petroleum Reporting Entity prepares a disclosure under the Petroleum Reporting Standard, what is expected for non-mandatory requirements, and what must the entity include in the disclosure if it does not follow a non-mandatory requirement?","A Petroleum Reporting Entity is expected to follow the Petroleum Reporting Standard not only for binding requirements but also, as a matter of regulatory expectation, for non-mandatory requirements; if it does not follow a non-mandatory requirement, it must transparently explain that departure within the disclosure itself. [#SRC:6604c89d-d79d-4a33-a77b-016d323c54fe] Specifically, the entity must fully comply with all binding requirements in the Petroleum Reporting Standard (including any tables, appendices, or schedules), and the Regulator expects full compliance with non-mandatory requirements unless the entity explains why it has not complied. [#SRC:6604c89d-d79d-4a33-a77b-016d323c54fe] Where the disclosure does not meet a non-mandatory requirement, the disclosure must include a statement describing both (i) how the disclosure differs from the relevant non-mandatory requirement and (ii) why it differs. [#TGT:47846bb1-a202-44c7-a042-465e8cf38dc6] This means the explanation is not optional or external: it must be included in the disclosure and must address the nature of the deviation and the rationale for it, tying the explanation to the relevant Petroleum Reporting Standard requirement that was not met. [#TGT:47846bb1-a202-44c7-a042-465e8cf38dc6]","Rule 12.2.1(1) requires a Petroleum Reporting Entity to fully comply with all binding requirements set out in the Petroleum Reporting Standard (including any tables, appendices or schedules).  The Regulator also expects a Petroleum Reporting Entity to fully comply with all non-mandatory requirements set out in the Petroleum Reporting Standard, or explain their non-compliance in accordance with Rule 12.2.2.","Requirements for all disclosures. Where a disclosure by a Petroleum Reporting Entity does not meet a non-mandatory requirement contained in the Petroleum Reporting Standard, the Petroleum Reporting Entity must provide in its disclosure a statement as to how and why its disclosure differs from the non-mandatory requirement contained in the relevant Petroleum Reporting Standard.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,6604c89d-d79d-4a33-a77b-016d323c54fe,47846bb1-a202-44c7-a042-465e8cf38dc6,,,12.2.2.Guidance,12.2.2,,,,,HV0018,15e360fdadbfb19a,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

13ac487b960f948c,"When an Authorised Person has a CR Exposure to a sovereign PSE in the UAE or another GCC jurisdiction, how should the firm determine whether it can treat that exposure like a central government/central bank exposure eligible for a 0% risk weight, including how the domestic-currency denomination and funding condition applies for individual Emirates of the UAE?","An Authorised Person should first determine whether the counterparty is a sovereign PSE in the UAE or GCC whose credit risk is comparable to its central government, because only those sovereign PSEs are eligible to be treated under the central-government-aligned approach described for such entities. [#SRC:81df5980-d082-4e25-8462-5f45542ef806] If that comparability condition is met, the next step is to assess whether the CR Exposure meets the denomination and funding requirements that govern when the central-government-aligned treatment applies; if it does, the sovereign PSE must be treated under the requirements applicable to that aligned treatment, and if it does not, it must instead be treated under the alternative treatment specified for cases where the denomination/funding condition is not satisfied. [#SRC:81df5980-d082-4e25-8462-5f45542ef806] In applying the denomination and funding condition, the firm may apply a 0% risk weight only where the CR Exposure is to a central government or central bank of a GCC member country and is both denominated and funded in that GCC member country’s domestic currency. [#TGT:0b38a29a-6f32-46d4-b772-9682878dc7c1] For exposures linked to the UAE, each individual Emirate must be treated as if it were its own GCC member country for purposes of assessing the domestic-currency denomination and funding requirement. [#TGT:0b38a29a-6f32-46d4-b772-9682878dc7c1]","In (1), sovereign PSEs in the UAE and GCC that exhibit Credit Risks comparable to their central government must be treated in accordance with the requirements set out in Rule 4.12.5, where they meet the requirements in relation to the denomination and funding of the CR Exposure, otherwise they must be treated in accordance with Rule 4.12.6(1).","Central government and central bank asset class. An Authorised Person may apply a 0% risk weight to any CR Exposure to central governments or central banks of a GCC member country which are denominated and funded in the domestic currency of the GCC member country. For the purposes of this Rule, individual Emirates of the UAE will be considered as though they were GCC member countries.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,81df5980-d082-4e25-8462-5f45542ef806,0b38a29a-6f32-46d4-b772-9682878dc7c1,,,4.12.6.(2),4.12.5,,,,,HV0019,13ac487b960f948c,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

3849236659a8948c,"How should a Listed Entity treat Securities for the purpose of counting against the relevant issuance limit when an earlier approval has lapsed, and what conditions would allow an unapproved issue (or agreement to issue) to be treated as approved—including any timing requirement for issuing the Securities after holders approve?","For counting against the relevant issuance limit, if an approval lapses, the Securities stop being treated as issued with that approval and must instead be counted within the pool of Relevant Issues for the limit calculation. [#SRC:76970fb8-577b-4a21-8996-4c8bde4ef2d2] Separately, an issue of, or agreement to issue, Securities that was made without approval can still be treated as having been made with approval for the same limit-calculation purpose, but only if all specified conditions are met. [#TGT:3f609871-988e-4e0c-921f-6e1066c630f6] Those conditions are: (i) the issue or agreement did not exceed the applicable limit; (ii) the holders of the Listed Entity’s Ordinary Securities subsequently approve the issue or agreement; and (iii) the Securities are issued within three months after the date of that subsequent approval. [#TGT:3f609871-988e-4e0c-921f-6e1066c630f6] In practical terms, a lapsed approval removes the ability to count the Securities as approved under that earlier approval, but a separate pathway exists to re-characterise an otherwise unapproved issue as approved—provided the limit was not exceeded and the post-approval issuance occurs within the three-month window. [#SRC:76970fb8-577b-4a21-8996-4c8bde4ef2d2] [#TGT:3f609871-988e-4e0c-921f-6e1066c630f6]","If the approval under Rule 9.7.5 lapses, the Securities can no longer be counted as Securities issued with approval under Rule 9.7.5 for the purposes of Rule 9.7.1 above, and instead are to be counted within Relevant Issues under Rule 9.7.1.","Subsequent approval of an issue of Securities. An issue of, or agreement to issue, Securities made without approval under Rule 9.7.1 is treated as having been made with approval for the purposes of Rule 9.7.1 if:

column2: the issue or agreement did not exceed the limit in Rule 9.7.1;
the holders of the Listed Entity’s Ordinary Securities subsequently approve it; and

the Securities are issued within three months of the date of the approval.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,76970fb8-577b-4a21-8996-4c8bde4ef2d2,3f609871-988e-4e0c-921f-6e1066c630f6,,,9.7.6.Guidance,9.7.5,,,,,HV0020,3849236659a8948c,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 7f383e197ff6f4e8,"When the Regulator holds Confidential Information that qualifies as CRD Information because it was received from an EEA Competent Authority, under what circumstances may the Regulator disclose it to facilitate the carrying out of a Public Function, and to which types of recipients can such a disclosure be made?","Where the Confidential Information is CRD Information—i.e., Confidential Information the Regulator received or obtained from an EEA Competent Authority by virtue of the Capital Requirements Directive—the Regulator’s ability to disclose it must be assessed in that specific context. [#SRC:dc3f77a8-19bb-49c7-a2f8-f257642a9321] An EEA Competent Authority is a public authority or body officially recognised under national law in an EEA jurisdiction and empowered to supervise institutions within the supervisory system. [#SRC:dc3f77a8-19bb-49c7-a2f8-f257642a9321] For disclosure to facilitate the carrying out of a Public Function, the Regulator may disclose Confidential Information where the disclosure is permitted or required under an enactment applicable to the Regulator (including applicable international obligations), or where it is made in good faith for the Regulator’s functions/powers or to further its objectives. [#TGT:c143e65b-358c-4ac8-855c-546a1c91e4d1] In addition, such disclosure may be made to specified categories of recipients to assist them in performing their functions and powers, including the ADGM Registrar of Companies, a Non-Abu Dhabi Global Market Regulator, relevant governmental/regulatory authorities (including for AML/CTF/sanctions), self-regulatory bodies for financial services, and criminal or civil law enforcement agencies (inside or outside the U.A.E.). [#TGT:c143e65b-358c-4ac8-855c-546a1c91e4d1]","The exceptions under section 199(1) of FSMR. The provisions in section 199(2) relate specifically to Confidential Information originating in another governmental or regulatory authority, or Confidential Information that is CRD Information, and provide for and are consistent with the exchange of information and professional secrecy requirements in the European Union’s Capital Requirements Directive.  For the purposes of section 199(2):

column2: ‘CRD Information’ is defined as Confidential Information received or obtained by the Regulator from the EEA Competent Authority by virtue of the Capital Requirements Directive; and

‘EEA Competent Authority’ means a public authority or body officially recognised by national law of a jurisdiction within the EEA and empowered by that national law to supervise institutions as part of the supervisory system.","Subject to subsection (2), the Regulator may disclose Confidential Information for the purpose of facilitating the carrying out of a Public Function where such disclosure is—
permitted or required under any enactment applicable to the Regulator, including, for the avoidance of doubt, any applicable international obligations;
made to—
the ADGM Registrar of Companies;
a Non-Abu Dhabi Global Market Regulator;

a governmental or regulatory authority exercising powers and performing functions relating to anti-money laundering, counter terrorist financing or sanctions compliance, whether in the Abu Dhabi Global Market or otherwise;
a self regulatory body or organisation exercising and performing powers and functions in relation to financial services, whether in the Abu Dhabi Global Market or otherwise;
a criminal law enforcement agency, whether in the U.A.E or otherwise, for the purpose of any criminal investigation or criminal proceedings; or
a civil law enforcement agency or body, whether in the Abu Dhabi Global Market, U.A.E or otherwise;

column1: for the purpose of assisting the performance by any such person of its functions and powers; or

column2: made in good faith for the purposes of the exercise of the functions and powers of the Regulator or in order to further the Regulator's objectives.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,dc3f77a8-19bb-49c7-a2f8-f257642a9321,c143e65b-358c-4ac8-855c-546a1c91e4d1,,,3.3.3,Part 16.199.(1),,,,,HV0021,7f383e197ff6f4e8,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 8619993885d71df5,"For an Authorised Person conducting Investment Business, which reconciliation and verification outputs must be captured for inclusion in the Resolution Pack, and what minimum frequencies apply to those underlying reconciliations and counts when Client Accounts are held with Third Party Agents and when Safe Custody Assets are involved?","An Authorised Person conducting Investment Business must ensure its Resolution Pack includes the most recent reconciliations relating to both Client Money and Client Investments, and those “most recent” items should be supported by the periodic reconciliation and counting processes required for Third Party Agent-held Client Accounts and Safe Custody Assets. [#SRC:803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5] In practice, this means the Resolution Pack should contain the latest completed reconciliation outputs for Client Money and Client Investments, reflecting the firm’s current position at the time the pack is assembled. [#SRC:803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5] To keep those reconciliation records current, the Authorised Person must operate (and therefore be able to evidence) at least the following minimum cycles: [#TGT:99a621ce-b3ab-4dbc-a9c7-eac1065776e6] - At least monthly, reconcile its records of Client Accounts held with Third Party Agents against the monthly statements received from those Third Party Agents. [#TGT:99a621ce-b3ab-4dbc-a9c7-eac1065776e6] - At least every six months, physically count all Safe Custody Assets held by the Authorised Person or its Nominee Company and reconcile that count to the Authorised Person’s records. [#TGT:99a621ce-b3ab-4dbc-a9c7-eac1065776e6] - At least every six months, reconcile individual Client ledger balances to the Authorised Person’s records of Safe Custody Assets balances held in Client Accounts. [#TGT:99a621ce-b3ab-4dbc-a9c7-eac1065776e6] Accordingly, the Resolution Pack’s reconciliation records should be the latest results produced by these required reconciliation/count routines. [#SRC:803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5]","The following records must be included in the Resolution Pack of an Authorised Person conducting Investment Business:

column2: Rules ‎2.7.1 and ‎3.7.1(d) (records of Client classification and Client agreements);
Rules 14.6.2 and ‎15.4.3 (master lists of all Client Accounts in relation to Client Money and Client investments);
Rule ‎15.4.4 and Rule ‎15.4.5 (adequate records and Client's written permission re use of Client Investments);
Rules 14.7.1 and 14.7.4 (assessment of appropriateness of Third-Party Agent and acknowledgement by Third-Party agent in respect of Client Money); and
Rule ‎15.5.1 and 15.6.1 (assessment of appropriateness of Third Party Agent and acknowledgement by Third-Party Agent in respect of Client Investments); and
Rule 14.11.1 and ‎15.9.1 (most recent reconciliations of Client Money and Client Investments).","An Authorised Person must:
at least every calendar month, reconcile its records of Client Accounts held with Third Party Agents with monthly statements received from those Third Party Agents;

at least every six months, count all Safe Custody Assets physically held by the Authorised Person, or its Nominee Company, and reconcile the result of that count to the records of the Authorised Person; and

at least every six months, reconcile individual Client ledger balances with the Authorised Person's records of Safe Custody Assets balances held in Client Accounts.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5,99a621ce-b3ab-4dbc-a9c7-eac1065776e6,,,16.4.1,15.9.1,,,,,HV0022,8619993885d71df5,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 0f560fde86dc4a4e,"When an Investigator needs access to a person’s business premises to inspect and copy documents, how can the Investigator compel entry through written notice, and what are the notice expectations regarding whether advance warning must be given (including when it may be appropriate not to give prior notice)?","An Investigator can compel access to business premises for inspection and copying of documents by issuing a written notice requiring the relevant person to permit entry to that person’s business premises during normal business hours for that purpose. [#TGT:ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046] The written notice power is not limited to the Person Under Investigation; it can be directed to the Person Under Investigation or to any other person, whether or not connected to the Person Under Investigation, so long as the notice requires permission for entry to that person’s business premises. [#TGT:ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046] Separately, where the Investigator exercises the power to enter business premises, the Investigator will give written notice of exercising that power, but the Investigator is not required to provide that notice in advance of the entry. [#SRC:36b4de81-9f09-4450-8fef-1fa5c5094980] In deciding whether to give prior notice of an inspection, the Investigator may consider circumstances where advance warning could prejudice the investigation; in such cases, the Investigator may consider it appropriate not to provide prior notice even though written notice of the exercise of the power is given. [#SRC:36b4de81-9f09-4450-8fef-1fa5c5094980]","Power to enter premises and inspect and copy documents . The Investigator will give written notice of the exercise of the power to enter business premises under section 206(1)(e) of FSMR. However, there is no requirement for an Investigator to give notice of the exercise of this power in advance. There may be circumstances when the Investigator considers it appropriate not to provide prior notice of an inspection, for example where the provision of prior notice may prejudice the investigation.","The Investigator may, by written notice, require the person who is the Person Under Investigation or any other person (whether or not connected to the Person Under Investigation) to—

column2: attend an interview at a Specified time and place and answer questions;
produce at a Specified time and place any Specified Documents or Documents of a Specified description;
provide such information as the Investigator may require;
provide such assistance as the Investigator may require; or

permit the Investigator to enter the business premises of such person during normal business hours for the purpose of inspecting and copying Documents on such premises.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,36b4de81-9f09-4450-8fef-1fa5c5094980,ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046,,,6.6.17,Part 17.206.(1),,,,,HV0023,0f560fde86dc4a4e,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 40961a2f7908a524,"When an Issuer wants a proposed Digital Security to be treated as a Security through the Regulator’s ability to deem an investment that is not a Security to be a Security, what information and documentation must the Issuer provide, and how does the Regulator’s review differ between a situation requiring an Approved Prospectus and an Exempt Offer (including what the review is not intended to do)?","If an Issuer seeks to have a proposed Digital Security treated as a Security through the Regulator’s discretion to deem an investment that is not a Security to be a Security (potentially on terms and conditions set by the Regulator), the Issuer should be prepared to provide information demonstrating that the proposed Digital Security meets the requirements of a Security. [#TGT:95497208-1e94-4b51-8ff3-d9e77f64177c] [#SRC:a8ffa89d-5c3e-41da-8f68-4b1795a0d986] In practice, the FSRA expects the Issuer to submit whatever information the FSRA requires to support that determination, focused on showing the Digital Security satisfies the applicable characteristics of a Security. [#SRC:a8ffa89d-5c3e-41da-8f68-4b1795a0d986] Where the circumstances require submission of an Approved Prospectus, the FSRA will rely on the documentation provided in that approval process as the basis for deciding whether to deem the Digital Security to be a Security. [#SRC:a8ffa89d-5c3e-41da-8f68-4b1795a0d986] Where the circumstances relate to an Exempt Offer, the FSRA will instead review the Exempt Offer documentation to enable it to make the deeming determination. [#SRC:a8ffa89d-5c3e-41da-8f68-4b1795a0d986] However, in the Exempt Offer context, the FSRA’s review is expressly not conducted to approve the Exempt Offer itself, even though the Regulator may attach terms and conditions to its deeming decision. [#SRC:a8ffa89d-5c3e-41da-8f68-4b1795a0d986] [#TGT:95497208-1e94-4b51-8ff3-d9e77f64177c]","REGULATORY TREATMENT OF DIGITAL SECURITIES

To use its powers under Section 58(2)(b), the FSRA expects that an Issuer will provide to it such information as is required to demonstrate that the proposed Digital Security meets the requirements of a “Security” (as defined in FSMR). In circumstances:

column2: requiring the submission of an Approved Prospectus to the FSRA, the FSRA will use the documentation submitted as part of this approval process to determine whether it will deem a Digital Security a Security under Section 58(2)(b) of FSMR; or

relating to an Exempt Offer, the FSRA will review the Exempt Offer documentation for the purposes of being able to make a determination under Section 58(2)(b).  The FSRA’s review will not be for the purposes of approving the Exempt Offer itself.","Without limiting the generality of its powers, the Regulator may, by written notice—
exclude the application of any requirements; or
deem any investment which is not a Security to be a Security for the purposes of these Regulations and the Rules made under these Regulations;

column1: subject to such terms and conditions as it may consider appropriate.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,a8ffa89d-5c3e-41da-8f68-4b1795a0d986,95497208-1e94-4b51-8ff3-d9e77f64177c,,,16),Part 6.Chapter 1.58.(2),,,,,HV0024,40961a2f7908a524,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,some_copied_acceptable,source_only_sufficient,

12a98ee480c6eb4d,"For a Listed Entity that qualifies for admission to the Official List and has an acceptable profitability or revenue track record (or substantial tangible assets with readily ascertainable value), how does the Regulator’s decision affect whether the APP 7 restriction categories apply, and which parties are within scope of the application provision when Securities are (or will be) treated as Restricted Securities?","Where a Listed Entity meets one of the stated admission-quality conditions (qualification for admission, an acceptable profitability or revenue track record, or substantial tangible assets with readily ascertainable value), the default position is that the specified APP 7 restriction categories are disapplied for that Listed Entity unless the Regulator decides otherwise. [#TGT:044c2eb2-828b-42a2-8b05-68613aed8eac] This means the Regulator retains discretion to re-impose those restriction categories even when the Listed Entity satisfies one of the conditions. [#TGT:044c2eb2-828b-42a2-8b05-68613aed8eac] In parallel, the application provision identifies who is covered when dealing with Securities that are, or will be, Restricted Securities: it applies to an Applicant for admission of Securities to the Official List, a relevant Listed Entity, and any Person who holds or will hold Securities that are Restricted Securities under APP 7 or that the Regulator has deemed to be Restricted Securities by notice to the relevant Applicant or Listed Entity. [#SRC:13cf0ba8-adc8-450e-bee1-619794cc9131] Accordingly, even if the Listed Entity benefits from the default disapplication of certain restriction categories, the scope of who is captured by the application provision still turns on whether the Securities are treated as Restricted Securities under APP 7 or by the Regulator’s notice. [#SRC:13cf0ba8-adc8-450e-bee1-619794cc9131]","Application. This section applies, subject to Rule 9.6.2, to:

column2: an Applicant for admission of Securities to the Official List;
a relevant Listed Entity; and

any Person that holds, or will hold, Securities that are Restricted Securities in accordance with APP 7 or which the Regulator has deemed to be Restricted Securities by giving notice to the relevant Applicant or Listed Entity.","Entry into Restriction Agreements and Application of Restriction. Unless the Regulator decides otherwise, the restrictions in categories 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 8 and 9 of APP 7 do not apply in relation to a Listed Entity that:
qualifies for admission to the Official List pursuant to Rule 2.3.15;
has a track record of profitability or revenue acceptable to the Regulator; or

in the opinion of the Regulator, has tangible assets with a readily ascertainable value which constitute a substantial proportion of the total value of its assets.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,13cf0ba8-adc8-450e-bee1-619794cc9131,044c2eb2-828b-42a2-8b05-68613aed8eac,,,9.6.1,9.6.2,,,,,HV0025,12a98ee480c6eb4d,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: b071d6d7145fe585,"When an Authorised Person wants to start offering Clients a Virtual Asset that was not originally approved in its application, what must it submit to the FSRA for approval, and how will the FSRA assess whether that Virtual Asset can be treated as an Accepted Virtual Asset for that Authorised Person?","An Authorised Person that intends to use a Virtual Asset in addition to the Accepted Virtual Asset(s) originally approved for it must obtain the FSRA’s approval before it offers that Virtual Asset to Clients. [#SRC:ee620070-0c48-454c-9530-0b3abf34c142] The approval request must be made in writing and include relevant information about the proposed use of the Virtual Asset, including the controls the Authorised Person has in place (or proposes to implement) to manage risks specific to that Virtual Asset. [#SRC:ee620070-0c48-454c-9530-0b3abf34c142] In assessing suitability, the FSRA will consider whether the proposed Virtual Asset meets the requirements to be an Accepted Virtual Asset, and an Accepted Virtual Asset status is demonstrated by, and applies to, that individual Authorised Person only (i.e., it is not automatically transferable across Authorised Persons). [#TGT:480fd476-0932-4064-b15a-5e2299439911] The FSRA’s assessment may take into account factors it considers relevant, including (at the date of the Guidance) maturity, security, traceability/monitoring, exchange connectivity, the type of distributed ledger used, innovation/efficiency, and practical application/functionality. [#TGT:480fd476-0932-4064-b15a-5e2299439911] The FSRA will then notify the Authorised Person of its determination. [#SRC:ee620070-0c48-454c-9530-0b3abf34c142]","REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR AUTHORISED PERSONS ENGAGED IN REGULATED ACTIVITIES IN RELATION TO VIRTUAL ASSETS

An Authorised Person wishing to use a Virtual Asset(s) additional to the Accepted Virtual Asset(s) originally approved as part of its application process, must first seek the FSRA’s approval before offering it to Clients.  This application should be made in writing and include all relevant information relating to the use of the Virtual Asset, including the relevant controls the Authorised Person has in place (or if not already in place, that it proposes to implement), in order to manage any risks specific to the Virtual Asset.
