As set out in paragraphs 16 and 32 of this Guidance, an Issuer wishing to make an Exempt Offer in order to have its Digital Securities admitted to trading on an MTF will need to ensure that it includes all required information in its Exempt Offer document in order to allow FSRA to deem the Digital Securities as Securities pursuant to section 58(2)(b) of FSMR.","Without limiting the generality of its powers, the Regulator may, by written notice—

column2: exclude the application of any requirements; or
deem any investment which is not a Security to be a Security for the purposes of these Regulations and the Rules made under these Regulations;

column1: subject to such terms and conditions as it may consider appropriate.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,1ad93605-b12d-4852-9c5f-18d8569c27a7,95497208-1e94-4b51-8ff3-d9e77f64177c,,,46),Part 6.Chapter 1.58.(2),,,,,HV0048,5da11b6862d3a3ee,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

3e2ee2e30ce215da,"For an Authorised Person conducting Investment Business, how should the Resolution Pack reflect the periodic reconciliation and counting activities required for Client Accounts held with Third Party Agents and for Safe Custody Assets (including any involvement of a Nominee Company), and what minimum frequencies apply?","An Authorised Person conducting Investment Business should ensure its Resolution Pack includes the most recent reconciliation records that evidence it is meeting the required reconciliation and counting cadence for Third Party Agent-held Client Accounts and for Safe Custody Assets. [#SRC:803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5] In practice, this means the pack should contain the latest reconciliations of Client Money and Client Investments, aligned to the underlying operational duties to (i) reconcile records of Client Accounts held with Third Party Agents against the Third Party Agents’ monthly statements at least every calendar month, and (ii) perform six‑monthly controls over Safe Custody Assets and related ledgers. [#SRC:803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5] [#TGT:99a621ce-b3ab-4dbc-a9c7-eac1065776e6] Specifically, the minimum frequencies that the reconciliation records in the pack should be capable of demonstrating are: - Monthly reconciliation of the Authorised Person’s records of Client Accounts held with Third Party Agents to the monthly statements received from those Third Party Agents. [#TGT:99a621ce-b3ab-4dbc-a9c7-eac1065776e6] - Six‑monthly physical count of all Safe Custody Assets held by the Authorised Person or its Nominee Company, reconciled back to the Authorised Person’s records. [#TGT:99a621ce-b3ab-4dbc-a9c7-eac1065776e6] - Six‑monthly reconciliation of individual Client ledger balances to the Authorised Person’s records of Safe Custody Assets balances held in Client Accounts. [#TGT:99a621ce-b3ab-4dbc-a9c7-eac1065776e6] Including the most recent reconciliations in the Resolution Pack provides the record set required for resolution readiness while reflecting these periodic control obligations. [#SRC:803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5]","The following records must be included in the Resolution Pack of an Authorised Person conducting Investment Business:

column2: Rules ‎2.7.1 and ‎3.7.1(d) (records of Client classification and Client agreements);
Rules 14.6.2 and ‎15.4.3 (master lists of all Client Accounts in relation to Client Money and Client investments);
Rule ‎15.4.4 and Rule ‎15.4.5 (adequate records and Client's written permission re use of Client Investments);
Rules 14.7.1 and 14.7.4 (assessment of appropriateness of Third-Party Agent and acknowledgement by Third-Party agent in respect of Client Money); and
Rule ‎15.5.1 and 15.6.1 (assessment of appropriateness of Third Party Agent and acknowledgement by Third-Party Agent in respect of Client Investments); and
Rule 14.11.1 and ‎15.9.1 (most recent reconciliations of Client Money and Client Investments).","An Authorised Person must:
at least every calendar month, reconcile its records of Client Accounts held with Third Party Agents with monthly statements received from those Third Party Agents;

at least every six months, count all Safe Custody Assets physically held by the Authorised Person, or its Nominee Company, and reconcile the result of that count to the records of the Authorised Person; and

at least every six months, reconcile individual Client ledger balances with the Authorised Person's records of Safe Custody Assets balances held in Client Accounts.",DPEL,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,803ff2b9-9528-459a-b9d2-45066785e9f5,99a621ce-b3ab-4dbc-a9c7-eac1065776e6,,,16.4.1,15.9.1,,,,,HV0049,3e2ee2e30ce215da,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 387a201e22438253,"If an Authorised Person uses the FCCA and has eligible financial Collateral for an SFT that is not under a qualifying bilateral Netting agreement, what number should it use instead of E for the credit risk weighted exposure, and how should it adjust for market moves in both the exposure and the collateral?","Where the Authorised Person has taken eligible financial Collateral for an SFT and that SFT is not covered by a qualifying bilateral Netting agreement, and the Authorised Person is using the FCCA, it must calculate an adjusted exposure amount (E*) and use that E* instead of E when working out the Credit Risk weighted Exposure amount for the relevant CR Exposure. [#SRC:99f36cb9-d6c3-4b1b-a90c-5d85b901b3de] This is not optional in the described circumstances: the calculation requires substituting E* for E in the credit risk weighting step. [#SRC:99f36cb9-d6c3-4b1b-a90c-5d85b901b3de] In calculating E* under the FCCA, the Authorised Person must build in the effect of possible future market-driven changes by adjusting both the size of the Exposure to the Counterparty and the value of any Collateral received that supports that Counterparty. [#TGT:2680d877-e922-4ecb-8fc1-60f4b4c13314] The adjustments must be made using the specified methods and haircuts designed to capture those potential fluctuations in exposure and collateral values. [#TGT:2680d877-e922-4ecb-8fc1-60f4b4c13314] The result is that the credit risk weighted exposure is based on an exposure measure that already reflects market-movement risk in both legs (exposure and collateral), rather than the unadjusted E. [#SRC:99f36cb9-d6c3-4b1b-a90c-5d85b901b3de] [#TGT:2680d877-e922-4ecb-8fc1-60f4b4c13314]","Measurement of E for pre settlement Counterparty Exposures arising from SFTs. An Authorised Person which has taken eligible financial Collateral for any SFT that is not covered by a qualifying bilateral Netting agreement and using the FCCA, must calculate E* in accordance with Rules A4.3.2 to A4.3.6 in App4, and substitute E* for E when calculating the Credit Risk weighted Exposure amount for that CR Exposure under Section 4.8.","Calculation of E* for collateralised transactions other than OTC Derivative transactions and long settlement transactions. An Authorised Person using the FCCA to calculate E* must adjust both the amount of the Exposure to the Counterparty and the value of any Collateral received in support of that Counterparty to take into account possible future fluctuations in the value of either due to market movements, by using the methods and haircuts set out in Rules A4.3.6 to A4.3.29.",DPEL,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,99f36cb9-d6c3-4b1b-a90c-5d85b901b3de,2680d877-e922-4ecb-8fc1-60f4b4c13314,,,4.9.19,APP4.A4.3.2,,,,,HV0050,387a201e22438253,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

53c811c6ecd14a10,"If a Fund Manager tells its auditor in writing to audit the Fund’s financial statements and to produce a Fund Auditor’s Report, what must the Fund Manager make sure the Auditor says in that report about the accounting standards used, whether the statements are true and fair, whether records were properly kept, whether the Auditor got enough information, and whether the Directors’ or Fund Manager’s report matches the financial statements?","The Fund Manager has to do more than simply appoint an auditor. It must, in writing, require its auditor to conduct an audit of the Fund’s financial statements in accordance with the relevant IAASB standards and to produce a Fund Auditor’s Report on the audited financial statements [#SRC:8949f938-33e5-4393-a256-021917125579]. Then, when it is procuring the production of that Fund Auditor’s Report, the Fund Manager must ensure the Auditor includes specific statements in the report. These include: whether the financial statements were properly prepared in line with the financial reporting standards adopted by the Fund; whether the statements give a true and fair view of the Fund’s financial position (including net income and net gains or losses of the Fund Property, or where relevant the Fund Property attributable to the Sub-Fund) for the annual accounting period and the position at the end of that period; whether proper accounting records have not been kept, or the statements do not agree with the accounting records and returns, or do not comply with applicable standards; whether the Auditor received all information and explanations needed for the audit; whether the information in the Directors’ report or the Fund Manager’s report is consistent with the financial statements; and any other required matter or opinion [#TGT:8a39a0f2-3ac3-4f8c-bf98-2752b5310cce].","Function of the Auditor. A Fund Manager must, in writing, require its auditor to:

column2: conduct an audit of the Fund's financial statements in accordance with the requirements of the relevant standards published by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB); and

produce a Fund Auditor's Report on the audited financial statements in accordance with GEN Rule 6.6.8.","Fund Auditor's Report. A Fund Manager must, in procuring the production of a Fund Auditor's Report, ensure that an Auditor states:
whether the financial statements have been properly prepared in accordance with the financial reporting standards adopted by the Fund in accordance with FUNDS;

whether the financial statements give a true and fair view of the financial position of the Fund, including the net income and the net gains or losses of the Fund Property, or, as the case may be, the Fund Property attributable to the Sub-Fund for the annual accounting period in question and the financial position of the Fund or Sub-Fund as at the end of the annual accounting period;

whether proper accounting records for the Fund, or as the case may be, Sub-Fund, have not been kept, or that the financial statements are not in agreement with the accounting records and returns, or that the financial statements do not comply with the applicable financial reporting standards;
whether it has been given all the information and explanations which, to the best of its knowledge and belief, are necessary for the purposes of its audit;
whether the information given in the report of the Directors or in the report of the Fund Manager for that period is consistent with the financial statements; and

any other matter or opinion required by FUNDS.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,8949f938-33e5-4393-a256-021917125579,8a39a0f2-3ac3-4f8c-bf98-2752b5310cce,,,PART 5.16.3.8,6.6.8,,,,,HV0051,53c811c6ecd14a10,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,target_only_sufficient,

column1: 96d798bb5745edb9,"In the annual report, what does the Reporting Entity need to say about who leads the Board and what decisions the Board keeps versus delegates to Senior Management, and what balance of skills and independence and what resources must the Board and its committees have for both the Reporting Entity and the Listed Entity?","The Reporting Entity’s annual report should name the key people in charge of governance and management—identifying the chairman, any deputy chairman, the Directors, and the chief executive—and it should also give a high-level explanation of which types of decisions are made by the Board and which are delegated to Senior Management [#SRC:35277484-31bd-49fe-956c-02f3ceff5405]. Alongside these disclosures, the Board and its committees must be set up and supported so they have an appropriate balance of skills, experience, independence, and knowledge of the entity’s business, and they must have adequate resources to do their work properly [#SRC:35277484-31bd-49fe-956c-02f3ceff5405]. Adequate resources include being able to access expertise when needed and receiving timely and comprehensive information about the affairs of the entity. The same expectation applies for the Listed Entity: its Board and committees must also maintain the appropriate balance and have adequate resources, including access to expertise and timely, comprehensive information relating to the Listed Entity’s affairs [#TGT:705e3965-3995-437d-abe7-8af619b6bbbb].","Chairman and Chief Executive. The annual report of the Reporting Entity should:

column2: identify the chairman, the deputy chairman (where there is one), the Directors and the chief executive; and
include a high level statement of which types of decisions are to be taken by the Board and which are to be delegated to the Senior Management.

column1: The Board and its committees must have an appropriate balance of skills, experience, independence and knowledge of the Reporting Entity's business, and adequate resources, including access to expertise as required and timely and comprehensive information relating to the affairs of the Reporting Entity.""","Principle 3 – Board composition and resources. The Board, and its committees, must have an appropriate balance of skills, experience, independence and knowledge of the Listed Entity's business, and adequate resources, including access to expertise as required and timely and comprehensive information relating to the affairs of the Listed Entity.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,35277484-31bd-49fe-956c-02f3ceff5405,705e3965-3995-437d-abe7-8af619b6bbbb,,,APP 4.20.,9.2.5,,,,,HV0052,96d798bb5745edb9,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,partial_unclear,too_much_copied_unnatural,both_needed,

c4c8063e2b10f8ea,"When setting expectations for a Reporting Entity’s Corporate Governance framework to support prudent and sound long‑term management in the interests of the Reporting Entity and its Shareholders, to what extent may the Regulator make Rules that prescribe Corporate Governance principles and standards and impose requirements on the Reporting Entity’s board of Directors and individual members, Controllers, employees, or other persons, including matters such as fair treatment of Shareholders and conflicts of interests?","The Regulator is permitted to use Rules to prescribe the Corporate Governance principles and standards that apply to a Reporting Entity, and those Rules may extend beyond high-level governance concepts to include specific requirements applicable to the Reporting Entity’s board of Directors and individual members, Controllers, employees, or any other person as appropriate. Those Rules may also cover requirements relating to fair treatment of Shareholders and provisions to address conflicts of interests, allowing the Regulator to translate governance expectations into concrete, role-specific obligations. This rulemaking permission operates in the context that the Regulator is entitled to enact rules requiring a Reporting Entity to have a Corporate Governance framework that is adequate to promote prudent and sound management of the Reporting Entity in the long-term interest of the Reporting Entity and its Shareholders. Taken together, the passages indicate that the Regulator can both require an adequate governance framework and prescribe detailed principles, standards, and related requirements to support that outcome. [#SRC:f3baa5a3-304f-41e2-b57d-97db937d12c1] [#TGT:d0183f42-1701-4885-9dcb-cb96c2d62d6d]","General. Section 73(2) of the FSMR provides that the Regulator is entitled to enact rules requiring a Reporting Entity to have a Corporate Governance framework which is adequate to promote prudent and sound management of the Reporting Entity in the long term interest of the Reporting Entity and its Shareholders. Accordingly, in providing its explanation in the annual report as noted in 2, a Reporting Entity should aim to illustrate how its actual practices achieve compliance with the outcomes intended by section 73 of the FSMR and the Principles, and thereby contribute to prudent and sound management of the Reporting Entity.","For the purposes of the requirement in subsection ‎(1), the Regulator may by Rules prescribe—

column2: Corporate Governance principles and standards that apply to a Reporting Entity, including any requirements applicable to its board of Directors and individual members, Controllers, employees or any other person as appropriate;
requirements relating to fair treatment of Shareholders; and

provisions to address conflicts of interests.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,f3baa5a3-304f-41e2-b57d-97db937d12c1,d0183f42-1701-4885-9dcb-cb96c2d62d6d,,,APP 4.3.,Part 6.Chapter 2.73.(2),,,,,HV0053,c4c8063e2b10f8ea,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 1d401bad230c5d15,"If an Investigator needs to go into someone’s business premises to look at and copy documents for an investigation, can the Investigator make the Person Under Investigation (or someone else) allow entry by sending a written notice, and does the visit have to be during normal business hours and only for documents relevant to the investigation?","Yes. The Investigator has permission to enter business premises to inspect and copy documents, but this is tied to the investigation: the documents inspected or copied must be relevant for the purposes of the investigation, and the entry is for that inspection-and-copying purpose [#SRC:6f288073-515c-4e53-9fa5-16c3700d2767]. Separately, the Investigator may, by written notice, require cooperation not only from the Person Under Investigation but also from any other person (even if not connected to the Person Under Investigation). One form of required cooperation is that the person must permit the Investigator to enter the person’s business premises during normal business hours so the Investigator can inspect and copy documents on those premises [#TGT:ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046]. Putting both together, the Investigator can use a written notice to require the person to allow entry, but the entry is limited to normal business hours under the notice and is limited in scope to inspecting and copying documents on-site that are relevant to the investigation.",Power to enter premises and inspect and copy documents . Section 206(1)(e) of FSMR permits the Investigator to enter business premises for the purpose of inspecting and copying any documents where relevant for the purposes of the investigation.,"The Investigator may, by written notice, require the person who is the Person Under Investigation or any other person (whether or not connected to the Person Under Investigation) to—

column2: attend an interview at a Specified time and place and answer questions;
produce at a Specified time and place any Specified Documents or Documents of a Specified description;
provide such information as the Investigator may require;
provide such assistance as the Investigator may require; or

permit the Investigator to enter the business premises of such person during normal business hours for the purpose of inspecting and copying Documents on such premises.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,6f288073-515c-4e53-9fa5-16c3700d2767,ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046,,,6.6.16,Part 17.206.(1),,,,,HV0054,1d401bad230c5d15,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 9dcca7d2db679059,"When an Authorised Person is monitoring and controlling its Exposures within the Large Exposures limits, what immediate notification and written follow-up obligations apply if (i) there is any breach of those limits and (ii) a Trading Book portion of a Large Exposure, alone or combined with any Non Trading Book portion, is likely to push the exposure above 25% of Tier 1, including what must be included in the notice to the Regulator?","An Authorised Person must operate controls that detect and respond promptly to limit issues while it monitors and controls Exposures on a daily basis within the Large Exposures limits [#SRC:29db355c-0b9a-45bd-af0b-0e40adbf1675]. If there is any breach of the limits, it must notify the Regulator immediately and then confirm that notification in writing [#SRC:29db355c-0b9a-45bd-af0b-0e40adbf1675]. Separately, where the Trading Book portion of a Large Exposure—either on its own or when added to any Non Trading Book portion—is likely to cause the 25% limit of the Authorised Person’s Tier 1 to be exceeded, the Authorised Person must immediately provide the Regulator with written notice [#TGT:74d112ce-e726-400a-9014-0a771a3717b8]. That written notice must explain the nature of the Trading Book Exposure and must seek specific guidance from the Regulator on the prudential treatment of the Exposure [#TGT:74d112ce-e726-400a-9014-0a771a3717b8]. Taken together, the firm should ensure immediate escalation to the Regulator for both actual breaches and likely exceedances, with written documentation that both confirms the breach notification and, where relevant, provides the required explanation and request for guidance.","Applicability and limits. For the purposes of this Section an Authorised Person must:

column2: identify its Exposures;
identify its Counterparties, including whether any are Closely Related to each other or Connected to the Authorised Person;
measure the size of its Exposures;
establish the value of its Exposures;
determine the size of its Exposures as a proportion of its Tier 1;
identify whether it has Exposures which are subject to the requirements of Section 4.13 (CRM);
identify which, if any, of its Exposures are exempt in accordance with Section A4.11 from the limits set out in Rules 4.15.4 to 4.15.7;
aggregate its Exposures to the same Counterparty or group of Closely Related Counterparties or group of Connected Counterparties;
monitor and control its Exposures on a daily basis within the Large Exposures limits; and

notify the Regulator immediately of any breach of the limits set out in this Section and confirm it in writing.","Large Exposures limits. Where the portion of a Large Exposure in an Authorised Person's Trading Book on its own or when added to any Non Trading Book portion of a Large Exposure, is likely to cause the 25% limit of its Tier 1 to be exceeded, the Authorised Person must immediately give the Regulator written notice, explaining the nature of its Trading Book Exposure and seeking specific guidance from the Regulator regarding the prudential treatment of any such Exposure.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,29db355c-0b9a-45bd-af0b-0e40adbf1675,74d112ce-e726-400a-9014-0a771a3717b8,,,4.15.3,4.15.6,,,,,HV0055,9dcca7d2db679059,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 09ed83603d5c9d13,"When preparing its Summary of Reserves and Resources, must a Petroleum Reporting Entity include the specified table in the prescribed form and within the stated timing window, and does that obligation apply if the Petroleum Reporting Entity is required to file SEC compliant Forms 10-K and 20-F Reports annually with the SEC?","A Petroleum Reporting Entity is generally required to include, within its Summary of Reserves and Resources, a table prepared in the form of MKT Form 12-1, and that table must be dated no earlier than one month before the Summary of Reserves and Resources is disclosed [#SRC:cd137cde-9ef8-4ed1-a401-6bf47f8ccb04]. However, the applicability of that requirement is limited for a Petroleum Reporting Entity that is required to file SEC compliant Forms 10-K and 20-F Reports annually with the SEC: such an entity is not required to comply with the underlying requirement that would otherwise impose the table-in-summary obligation [#TGT:b249219a-57ec-4b15-be46-58475357c6c1]. In practice, this means you should first determine whether the entity falls within the SEC annual filing category described; if it does, the entity is carved out from having to comply with the requirement that mandates inclusion of the MKT Form 12-1 table and its associated “no earlier than one month” dating constraint. If it does not, the entity must include the table and meet the timing condition when disclosing the Summary.","Subject to Rule 12.14.3, a Petroleum Reporting Entity must include in its Summary of Reserves and Resources a table in the form of MKT Form 12-1, as of a date no earlier than one month prior to the disclosure of the Summary of Reserves and Resources.",A Petroleum Reporting Entity that is required to file SEC compliant Forms 10-K and 20-F Reports annually with the SEC is not required to comply with Rule 12.14.1.,SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,cd137cde-9ef8-4ed1-a401-6bf47f8ccb04,b249219a-57ec-4b15-be46-58475357c6c1,,,12.14.1,12.14.3,,,,,HV0056,09ed83603d5c9d13,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

343c7ec7230ec8a7,"If a Listed Entity had an approval for Securities but that approval later lapses, can it still treat those Securities as approved when working out Relevant Issues and whether it must not issue more Equity Securities without approval from holders of Ordinary Securities?","No. If the approval lapses, the Securities affected can no longer be treated as Securities issued with approval for the purpose of the counting exercise, and they must instead be counted within Relevant Issues [#SRC:76970fb8-577b-4a21-8996-4c8bde4ef2d2]. This directly affects the restriction on new issues because a Listed Entity must not issue, or agree to issue, more Equity Securities than the maximum number calculated by the formula unless it has the approval of the holders of Ordinary Securities [#TGT:a5d5f764-a746-4801-8e14-9584a84d3933]. The formula subtracts Relevant Issues from 20% of the Base Amount, so adding these Securities into Relevant Issues reduces the maximum number the Listed Entity can issue or agree to issue without holder approval [#TGT:a5d5f764-a746-4801-8e14-9584a84d3933]. Practically, once the approval has lapsed, the Listed Entity must recalculate using the revised Relevant Issues figure and ensure it does not proceed with any issue or agreement that would exceed the recalculated maximum unless it first obtains holder approval [#SRC:76970fb8-577b-4a21-8996-4c8bde4ef2d2] [#TGT:a5d5f764-a746-4801-8e14-9584a84d3933].","If the approval under Rule 9.7.5 lapses, the Securities can no longer be counted as Securities issued with approval under Rule 9.7.5 for the purposes of Rule 9.7.1 above, and instead are to be counted within Relevant Issues under Rule 9.7.1.","Restrictions on new Issues of Equity Securities . A Listed Entity must not issue, or agree to issue, more Equity Securities than the number calculated according to the following formula, without the approval of the holders of Ordinary Securities:
Maximum number of Equity Securities = (20% * Base Amount) – Relevant Issues),
Base Amount = the number of fully paid Ordinary Securities on issue as of the date 12 months before the date of issue or agreement (the “12 months Base Amount”), plus the number of:

column2: fully paid Ordinary Securities issued in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement under an exception in Rule 9.7.4 other than exceptions (8), (15) or (16);
fully paid Ordinary Securities issued in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement under an exception in Rule 9.7.4 other than exception (15), where the agreement was:
entered into before the commencement of the 12 month period; or
approved, or taken under the Rules to have been approved, under Rule 9.7.1 or Rule 9.7.5; and
any other fully paid Ordinary Securities issued in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement with approval under Rule 9.7.1 or Rule 9.7.5;

column1: The Base Amount may include fully paid Ordinary Securities issued in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement under an agreement to issue Securities within Rule 9.7.4 exception (14) where the issue is subsequently approved under Rule 9.7.1.

column2: partly paid Ordinary Securities that became fully paid in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement,

column1: but subtracting the number of fully paid Ordinary Securities cancelled in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement.
Relevant Issues = the number of Equity Securities issued, or agreed to be issued, in the 12 months before the date of issue or agreement to issue other than:

column2: with the approval of the holders of its Ordinary Securities under Rule 9.7.1 or Rule 9.7.5; or

under an exception in Rule 9.7.4.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,76970fb8-577b-4a21-8996-4c8bde4ef2d2,a5d5f764-a746-4801-8e14-9584a84d3933,,,9.7.6.Guidance,9.7.1,,,,,HV0057,343c7ec7230ec8a7,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 51d9cf72aea6f0f0,"When a Mining Reporting Entity makes a disclosure that includes forecast financial information derived from a Production Target and also includes ore reserves information supported by a separate report annexed to the disclosure, what must the Mining Reporting Entity include about the assumptions used to determine the forecast financial information, and how must the ore reserves information in the disclosure be presented relative to the separate report?","Where a Mining Reporting Entity’s disclosure contains forecast financial information derived from a Production Target, it must include comprehensive information about the assumptions used to determine that forecast financial information: all material economic assumptions employed; if it considers those material economic assumptions commercially sensitive, it must state that and explain the methodology used to determine them; and it must also include all other material assumptions utilised, together with the Production Target from which the forecast financial information is derived (including the required accompanying information) [#SRC:2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489]. In the same disclosure, if ore reserves information is included and a separate report is prepared and included as an annexure, the information included in the disclosure must be a fair and balanced representation of the information contained in that separate report [#TGT:b8cb4fdb-f627-43ae-90bf-801a549f8d63]. In meeting this obligation, the Mining Reporting Entity is not expected to summarise all information in the separate report; instead, it should include only information that is material to understanding the estimates of Mineral Resources in the separate report and that is not otherwise included in the body of the disclosure [#TGT:b8cb4fdb-f627-43ae-90bf-801a549f8d63].","A Mining Reporting Entity’s disclosure pursuant to Rule 11.9.1 must include:

column2: in relation to the assumptions used to determine the forecast financial information:
all material economic assumptions employed;

if the Mining Reporting Entity considers the material economic assumptions to be commercially sensitive, a statement to that effect and an explanation of the methodology used to determine the material economic assumptions; and

column1: A Mining Reporting Entity that considers certain information relating to the material economic assumptions to be commercially sensitive should refer to paragraphs 47-54 of the Guidance on Mining and paragraphs 127 and 128 of the Guidance on Continuous Disclosure.

column2: all other material assumptions utilised.

the Production Target from which the forecast financial information is derived (including all the information contained in Rule 11.8.3).","ORE RESERVES . Pursuant to Rule 11.6.1, the information included in the disclosure must be a fair and balanced representation of the information contained in the separate report prepared in accordance with Rule 11.6.2 (which must be included as an annexure to the disclosure).  In complying with this obligation, the FSRA does not expect a Mining Reporting Entity to prepare a summary of all the information contained in the separate report.  Instead, it is expected that that only information which is material to understanding the estimates of Mineral Resources contained in the separate report, that is not otherwise included in the body of the disclosure, be included.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489,b8cb4fdb-f627-43ae-90bf-801a549f8d63,,,11.9.2,48),,,,,HV0058,51d9cf72aea6f0f0,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: dd9324192c9a7188,"When determining the Credit RWA of an Authorised Person as an aggregate sum that includes the component for Credit Risk Exposures, what calculation steps must the Authorised Person follow to compute and aggregate the RWA for all of its CR Exposures so that this component can be included in the overall Credit RWA total?","Credit RWA for an Authorised Person is defined as an overall total made up of multiple components, including the risk weighted assets for all of its Credit Risk Exposures (CR Exposures) as one of the summed elements [#SRC:5e5b0814-b3c0-441d-b92e-c7fe290a8020]. To produce that CR Exposures component for inclusion in the total, the Authorised Person must calculate RWA for CR Exposures by applying a defined sequence: first determine the Exposure value (E) for every on-balance sheet and off balance sheet asset using the specified exposure measurement methodology and recognising the effects of any applicable CRM; then categorise each Exposure under the applicable rules; then allocate the applicable Credit Quality Grade and risk weight for each Exposure; then compute the RWA amount for each CR Exposure using the formula RWA(CR) = E × CRW, where CRW is the applicable risk weight determined through the categorisation and grading steps; and finally add together the RWA amounts for all CR Exposures to arrive at the aggregate RWA for CR Exposures [#TGT:5c99a9f9-b97d-4f45-834a-0562c13cf368].","The Credit RWA of an Authorised Person is the sum of:

column2: its risk weighted assets (RWA) for all its Credit Risk Exposures (referred to in these Rules as ""CR Exposures"") calculated in accordance with Rules 4.8.2 and 4.8.3;
its RWA for all its securitisation Exposures (referred to in these Rules as ""SE Exposures"") calculated in accordance with Rule 4.8.4 and Section 4.14; and

its RWA for its Counterparty Risk Exposures as calculated in accordance with Sections A4.6 to A4.8.","Calculation of RWA for Credit Risk Exposures (CR Exposures). To calculate its RWA for CR Exposures, an Authorised Person must:

calculate the value of the Exposure (represented as ""E"") for every on-balance sheet and every off balance sheet asset in accordance with the Exposure measurement methodology specified in Section 4.9 and recognising the effects of any applicable CRM;
categorise that Exposure in accordance with the Rules in Section 4.10;
allocate an applicable Credit Quality Grade and risk weight for that Exposure in accordance with the Rules in Section 4.11 and 4.12;
calculate the RWA amount for that Exposure using the following formula: RWA(CR) = E x CRW
RWA(CR)"" refers to the risk weighted Exposure amount for that CR Exposure;
E"" refers to the Exposure value or amount, for that CR Exposure; and
CRW"" refers to the applicable risk weight for that CR Exposure determined in accordance with (b) and (c); and

add the RWA amounts calculated in accordance with (d) for all its CR Exposures.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,5e5b0814-b3c0-441d-b92e-c7fe290a8020,5c99a9f9-b97d-4f45-834a-0562c13cf368,,,4.8.1.(2),4.8.3,,,,,HV0059,dd9324192c9a7188,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 301d53276af79a92,"If the Fund Manager of a Passported Fund has to tell the Regulator about a material event as soon as practicable (and within the stated deadline once it becomes aware), what details must be included with the notice, and what extra document is required if the Prospectus has been amended or replaced?","When the Fund Manager of a Passported Fund (and, where applicable, the governing body or trustee) must notify the Regulator of a material event as soon as practicable—and for the listed events no later than seven days after it becomes aware—the notice must be submitted in the prescribed form that the Regulator may direct from time to time [#TGT:7a51b100-c0e6-41bd-809c-d2ae395a9898] [#SRC:a293c037-9b5d-4128-8318-f840f0264d1f]. The notice cannot be just a headline: at a minimum it must be accompanied by reasonable detail of the event, so the Regulator receives enough information about what happened (for example, the nature of the change or occurrence and what it affects) [#SRC:a293c037-9b5d-4128-8318-f840f0264d1f]. If the event being notified is that the Prospectus relating to the Passported Fund has been amended or replaced, the notice must also include a copy of the new Prospectus, so the Regulator receives the updated or replacement Prospectus alongside the notification [#TGT:7a51b100-c0e6-41bd-809c-d2ae395a9898] [#SRC:a293c037-9b5d-4128-8318-f840f0264d1f].","The notification referred to in Rule 6.6.2 must be in such prescribed form as the Regulator may direct from time to time.  At a minimum, the notification must be accompanied by reasonable detail of the event and (where the Prospectus has been amended or replaced) a copy of the new Prospectus.","The Fund Manager of a Passported Fund must notify the Regulator as soon as practicable of any material events, in accordance with applicable ADGM legislation.  In particular (but without limitation), a Fund Manager or the governing body or trustee of a Passported Fund must notify the Regulator as soon as practicable (and in any case no later than seven days after it becomes aware) of any of the following events:

column2: the Fund Manager intends to retire as manager of the Passported Fund;
it is proposed that a successor manager will be appointed in relation to the Passported Fund;
the Fund Manager has been removed or replaced as manager of the Passported Fund;
any material service provider to the Passported Fund (including, without limitation, any custodian) or an Agent or Licensed Person resigns, is appointed, is removed, or is replaced;
the Prospectus relating to the Passported Fund has been amended or replaced;
winding-up of the Passported Fund has commenced; or

the Fund Manager intends to vary or revoke its Financial Service Permission (or any conditions contained in that Financial Service Permission).",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,a293c037-9b5d-4128-8318-f840f0264d1f,7a51b100-c0e6-41bd-809c-d2ae395a9898,,,6.6.3,6.6.2,,,,,HV0060,301d53276af79a92,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 3a9f52453ae801bb,"When a Relevant Person has maintained records relating to customer due diligence, customer business relationships, transactions, and suspicious activity reporting, what must it do if the Regulator requests a copy of the relevant record, and how does this interact with the requirement to keep those records for a minimum retention period?","A Relevant Person must ensure it both (i) keeps the specified categories of records for the required retention period and (ii) can produce the relevant record promptly when demanded. Specifically, it must, where relevant, maintain records covering documents and information obtained for initial and ongoing CDD or due diligence on business partners; records (originals or certified copies) relating to the customer business relationship (including business correspondence, information relating to a customer’s account, and sufficient transaction records to reconstruct individual transactions); internal findings and analysis for unusual or suspicious transactions or business; internal notifications to its MLRO; Suspicious Activity/Transaction Reports with supporting materials; communications with the FIU; and other expressly required matters, for at least six years from the latest of the report/notification date, the end of the business relationship, or completion of the transaction [#TGT:2bb23374-a3ae-4dd1-af3e-7222ecda1e98]. In addition, upon request, it must immediately provide to the Regulator a copy of the relevant record, and it must likewise provide it to a law enforcement agency where there is a valid and enforceable request or requirement [#SRC:c96c05de-76d2-4f05-b2ea-6f4fb9615094].","A Relevant Person must immediately provide to the Regulator, upon request, or a law enforcement agency, pursuant to a valid and enforceable request or requirement, a copy of the record referred to in Rule 4.5.1.","A Relevant Person must, where relevant, maintain the following records:

column2: a copy of all documents and information obtained in undertaking initial and ongoing CDD or due diligence on business partners;
records, consisting of the original documents or certified copies, in respect of the customer business relationship, including:
business correspondence and other information relating to a customer’s account;
sufficient records of transactions to enable individual transactions to be reconstructed; and

internal findings and analysis relating to a transaction or any business, if the transaction or business appears unusual or suspicious, whether or not it results in a Suspicious Activity/Transaction Report;
internal notifications of suspicious activity made to its MLRO under Rule ‎‎14.2.2;
Suspicious Activity/Transaction Reports and any relevant supporting documents and information, including internal findings and analysis;
any relevant communications with the FIU;
the documents in Rule ‎4.6.1; and
any other matter that the Relevant Person is expressly required to record under these Rules,

column1: for at least six years from the date on which the notification or report was made, the business relationship ends or the Transaction is completed, whichever occurs last.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,c96c05de-76d2-4f05-b2ea-6f4fb9615094,2bb23374-a3ae-4dd1-af3e-7222ecda1e98,,,4.5.2,4.5.1,,,,,HV0061,3a9f52453ae801bb,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

a806d0f5b2bb456a,"When preparing the weekly position report that a Recognised Investment Exchange must publish and provide to the Regulator for each Derivative admitted to trading, how must the Recognised Investment Exchange distinguish, as far as practicable, between risk-reducing positions tied directly to commercial activities and other positions, while still reporting the required aggregate position details by category of participant?","A Recognised Investment Exchange must produce a weekly position report that is both (i) publicly disclosed and provided to the Regulator and (ii) structured so that positions are separated, to the extent possible, into those that objectively reduce risks directly relating to commercial activities versus other positions. In practice, this means the Recognised Investment Exchange must categorise persons into participant categories and then, within the weekly reporting process, differentiate positions along the two position types while still presenting the report as aggregate positions held by each category of participant for each Derivative admitted to trading. The weekly report must detail, for each relevant category and Derivative, the number of long and short positions, changes since the previous report, the percentage of total open interest represented by each category, and the number of persons holding a position in each category. These content elements must be delivered in the same weekly report that is made public and provided to the Regulator, while the differentiation requirement ensures the report distinguishes risk-reducing commercial positions from other positions as far as practicable. [#SRC:2722b40a-c3fd-4d87-a5aa-65796ac6bdf2] [#TGT:ce2f97e5-2183-47cc-a1b0-23f2db75b226]","Position Reports. For the weekly report referred to under Rule 3.3.12, the Recognised Investment Exchange must:

column2: categorise persons in accordance with Rule 3.3.15; and
differentiate, to the extent possible, between positions identified as:
positions which in an objectively measurable way reduce risks directly relating to commercial activities; and

other positions.","Position Reports. A Recognised Investment Exchange must make public, and provide to the Regulator, a weekly report detailing the aggregate positions held by each category of participant for each Derivative that is admitted to trading on the Recognised Investment Exchange, specifying:
the number of long and short positions by such categories;
any changes in positions since the previous report;
the percentage of the total open interest represented by each category of participant; and

the number of persons holding a position in each category of participant.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,2722b40a-c3fd-4d87-a5aa-65796ac6bdf2,ce2f97e5-2183-47cc-a1b0-23f2db75b226,,,3.3.14,3.3.12,,,,,HV0062,a806d0f5b2bb456a,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: cee4e7c62e8f66ca,"When a Payment Service User requests information at any time during the term of a Framework Contract, what information must the Payment Service Provider provide, and how does that obligation relate to the minimum information that the Framework Contract itself must include unless the Payment Service Provider and a Payment Service User which is not a Natural Person agree otherwise in writing?","If the Payment Service User requests it at any time during the term of the Framework Contract, the Payment Service Provider must provide (i) the information that the Framework Contract is required to include as its mandatory content (unless the parties have otherwise agreed in writing where the Payment Service User is not a Natural Person) and (ii) any other terms of the Framework Contract beyond that mandatory content. In practice, this means the Payment Service Provider must be able to supply, on request, the full set of required Framework Contract disclosures—covering information about the Payment Service Provider, the Payment Service, charges and exchange rates, communications, safeguards and corrective measures, changes and termination, redress, and (where applicable) Stored Value redemption—together with any additional contractual terms the parties have included. The written “otherwise agreed” carve-out for a Payment Service User which is not a Natural Person affects what must be included as mandatory information in the Framework Contract, but it does not remove the Payment Service Provider’s duty to provide the information that is specified for provision on request, plus the remaining contractual terms, during the contract term. [#SRC:297c1b5c-a066-4f82-b626-7572c7d5de26] [#TGT:08c0ad25-70d0-4613-863a-43b760cfd83b]","If the Payment Service User so requests at any time during the term of the Framework Contract, the Payment Service Provider must provide the information specified in Rule 19.2.1 as well as any other terms of the Framework Contract.

Changes in contractual information","Unless otherwise agreed in writing by a Payment Service Provider and a Payment Service User which is not a Natural Person in accordance with Rule 19.6.1, a Framework Contract between a Payment Service Provider and a Payment Service User must include the following information:

column2: about the Payment Service Provider:
the name of the Payment Service Provider;
the address and contact details of the Payment Service Provider’s office in ADGM;
the name of the Regulator of the Payment Service Provider, and details of the Payment Service Provider’s Financial Service Permission;
about the Payment Service:
a description of the main characteristics of the Payment Service to be provided;
the information or unique identifier that must be provided by the Payment Service User in order for a Payment Order to be properly initiated and executed;
the form and procedure for giving consent to the initiation of a Payment Order or execution of a Payment Transaction and for the withdrawal of consent in accordance with Rule 19.10.1(3);
the time of receipt of a Payment Order, in accordance with Rule 19.14.1, and the cut-off time for the processing of a Payment Order, if any, established by the Payment Service Provider;
the maximum execution time for the Payment Services to be provided; and
any spending limits for the use of a Payment Instrument as agreed in accordance with Rule 19.10.2(1);
about charges and exchange rates:

details of all charges payable by the Payment Service User to the Payment Service Provider, including those connected to information which is provided or made available and, where applicable, a breakdown of the amounts of all charges;
where relevant, details of the exchange rates to be applied or, if Reference Exchange Rates are to be used, the method of calculating the relevant date for determining such Reference Exchange Rates;
where relevant and if agreed, the application of changes in Reference Exchange Rates and information requirements relating to any such changes, in accordance with Rule 19.2.5;
about communication:

the means of communication agreed between the parties for the transmission of information or notifications including, where relevant, any technical requirements for the Payment Service User’s equipment and software for receipt of the information or notifications;
the manner in which and frequency with which information under Chapter 19 is to be provided or made available;
the Payment Service User’s right to receive the revised terms of the Framework Contract and any other information in accordance with Rule 19.2.4;
about safeguards and corrective measures:

where relevant, a description of the steps that the Payment Service User must to take in order to keep safe a Payment Instrument and how to notify the Payment Service Provider of loss of the Payment Instrument for the purposes of Rule 19.11.1(3);
how and within what period of time the Payment Service User must notify the Payment Service Provider of any unauthorised or incorrectly initiated or executed Payment Transaction under Rule 19.17.1;
the secure procedure by which the Payment Service Provider will contact the Payment Service User in the event of suspected or actual fraud or security threats;
where relevant, the conditions under which the Payment Service Provider proposes to reserve the right to stop or prevent the use of a Payment Instrument in accordance with Rule 19.14.2;
the Payer’s liability under Rule 19.20.1 including details of any limits on such liability;
the Payment Service Provider’s liability for unauthorised Payment Transactions under Rule 19.20.1;
the Payment Service Provider’s liability for the initiation or execution of Payment Transactions under Rule 19.21.2 or Rule 19.21.3; and
the conditions for the payment of any refund to the Payment Service User under this Chapter.
about changes to and termination of the Framework Contract:

where relevant, the proposed terms under which the Payment Service User will be deemed to have accepted changes to the Framework Contract in accordance with Rule 19.2.5, unless they notify the Payment Service Provider that they do not accept such changes before the proposed date of their entry into force;
the duration of the Framework Contract;
where relevant, the right of the Payment Service User to terminate the Framework Contract and any agreements relating to termination in accordance with Rule 19.2.8.
about redress:
any contractual clauses on the law applicable to the Framework Contract and the competent courts; and
the availability of any alternative dispute resolution procedures, if applicable,  for the Payment Service User and the methods for having access to them.

if the Payment Service involves the issuance of Stored Value, about the redemption of Stored Value, including the conditions of redemption and any related Fees.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,297c1b5c-a066-4f82-b626-7572c7d5de26,08c0ad25-70d0-4613-863a-43b760cfd83b,,,19.2.3,19.2.1,,,,,HV0063,cee4e7c62e8f66ca,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 6110e9833cd25477,"If a Relevant Person is assessing a customer and deciding whether to rate them high risk because of the countries involved, what kinds of reports and organisations count as credible sources for deciding that a country has weak anti-money laundering controls, high corruption or crime, sanctions exposure, or terrorism links?","A Relevant Person must, when carrying out a risk-based assessment of a customer and deciding whether to assign a high-risk rating, consider all relevant risk factors that reasonably apply to the customer, including geographical or jurisdictional risk factors about the countries connected to the customer [#TGT:938ee9c6-a91c-4702-9039-d34906f00b5c]. Those country factors include whether countries are identified by credible sources as not having effective systems to counter money laundering, not implementing measures consistent with FATF Recommendations, having significant corruption or other criminal activity (including terrorism, money laundering, or illicit drugs), being subject to sanctions or similar measures, providing funding or support for terrorism, or having organisations designated as terrorist organisations operating in their territory [#TGT:938ee9c6-a91c-4702-9039-d34906f00b5c]. For deciding what counts as a “credible source” for these purposes, credible sources include (but are not limited to) mutual evaluations and detailed assessment or follow-up reports issued by FATF, the International Monetary Fund (IMF), the World Bank, the OECD, and other International Organisations [#SRC:d9e3fef9-b049-4b8f-9140-4d98002c3dab]. So, the Relevant Person should rely on these kinds of reports and issuers when identifying higher-risk countries and then factor that into the customer’s overall risk rating decision [#TGT:938ee9c6-a91c-4702-9039-d34906f00b5c] [#SRC:d9e3fef9-b049-4b8f-9140-4d98002c3dab].","For the purposes of ‎7.1.2(1)(c), a credible source includes, but is not limited to, mutual evaluations, detailed assessment reports or follow-up reports issued by FATF, the International Monetary Fund (“IMF”), the World Bank, the OECD and other International Organisations.","When undertaking a risk-based assessment of a customer and considering whether or not to assign a high-risk rating under ‎7.1.1(1)(b), a Relevant Person must take into account all relevant risk factors that would reasonably apply to the customer, including but not limited to:

column2: customer risk factors, including whether the:
business relationship is conducted in unusual circumstances;

payments will be received from unknown or unassociated third parties;
the service involves the provision of nominee directors, nominee shareholders or shadow directors, or the formation of companies in another country;

are identified by credible sources as providing funding or support for terrorism;

have organisations operating within their territory that have been designated by the State, other countries or International Organisations as terrorist organisations.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,d9e3fef9-b049-4b8f-9140-4d98002c3dab,938ee9c6-a91c-4702-9039-d34906f00b5c,,,7.1.2.(2),7.1.2.(1),,,,,HV0064,6110e9833cd25477,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 5b25e6b288de8e80,"If the Fund Manager of a Public Fund tells the Regulator it wants the Public Fund to be a Passported Fund, what must it do if it later finds a significant change, mistake, or missing information that matters to that notice before Promotion starts in a Host Jurisdiction, and what will the Regulator do next?","After the Fund Manager of a Public Fund decides to use the passporting procedures and notifies the Regulator that it intends the Public Fund to be a Passported Fund [#TGT:9ca2c478-4456-4c79-b447-743632309a37], it has an ongoing duty to address problems that could affect that notice. If, in the period after that notification and before Promotion begins in a Host Jurisdiction, the Fund Manager becomes aware of any material change, error, or omission that is reasonably likely to be relevant to what it told the Regulator, the Fund Manager must send the Regulator a written notice without delay [#SRC:b27b7465-dcf2-43cf-a342-6f999ce5dadc]. This requirement applies when the issue is important (material) and when it is reasonably likely to matter to the earlier notification, and it applies whether the issue is new information, a correction of a mistake, or filling in something that was left out. Once the Regulator receives that written notice, it will promptly pass all relevant details of the material change, error, or omission to the relevant Host Regulator [#SRC:b27b7465-dcf2-43cf-a342-6f999ce5dadc].","If, at any time between the notification pursuant to Rule 3.2.2 and the commencement of Promotion in a Host Jurisdiction, the Fund Manager becomes aware of any material change, error, or omission reasonably likely to be relevant to such notification, the Fund Manager shall give written notice to the Regulator without delay.  The Regulator will promptly provide the relevant Host Regulator with all relevant details of the material change, error or omission.","If the Fund Manager of a Public Fund wishes to use the passporting procedures under these Rules, it must notify the Regulator of its intention that the Public Fund be a Passported Fund.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,b27b7465-dcf2-43cf-a342-6f999ce5dadc,9ca2c478-4456-4c79-b447-743632309a37,,,3.2.9,3.2.2,,,,,HV0065,5b25e6b288de8e80,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

ebd9610d5d4d47a7,"If an Authorised Person decides to lower the value of its Exposures using credit risk mitigation options like provisions, netting, collateral, guarantees, credit derivatives, or securitisation, what policy must it write down about using any exclusions, and how does that fit with the fact the reductions are optional?","An Authorised Person is allowed to reduce the value of its Exposures, and it can choose to do so at its discretion, by using one or more listed credit risk mitigation approaches. These include reducing by specific provisions tied to credit loss risk (and not general reserves), netting claims and liabilities to a Counterparty if the stated conditions are met, recognising eligible Collateral that meets the stated type and requirements, recognising eligible guarantees, recognising qualifying Credit Derivatives that meet the stated conditions, and recognising securitisation transactions that transfer Credit Risks if the stated conditions are met [#TGT:9ae2763f-2e1a-4afb-ac8e-f57ce03a81c3]. Even though using these reductions is optional, the Authorised Person still has a mandatory governance step: it must document its policy for how it will use any exclusions that apply within this recognition framework [#SRC:5a4ad383-0e7b-476f-84ee-d6bce45b2270]. So, discretion applies to whether and which mitigation methods are used, but documentation is required to control and evidence how exclusions are applied when the Authorised Person uses them.",Recognition of Credit Risk mitigations. An Authorised Person must document its policy for the use of any of the exclusions in Rule 4.15.12.,"Recognition of Credit Risk mitigations. For the purposes of this Section, an Authorised Person may reduce the value of its Exposures, at its discretion, by any one or more of the following:

column2: the amount of any specific provision made, where the provision relates to the risk of a credit loss occurring on that Exposure and is not held as part of a general provision or reserve against its Credit Risks;
Netting its claims on and liabilities to a Counterparty, provided that the conditions in Section 4.13 of CRM are met;
the amount of Collateral held against its Exposures, where that Collateral is of a type listed based on the FCSA and FCCA approaches and meeting the requirements under Section 4.13;
the amount of any eligible guarantees as permitted under Section 4.13.9;
the value of a Credit Derivative, where the Credit Derivative is an instrument included in Rule 4.13.11 and the transaction meets the conditions set out in that Section; and

the effects of transactions transferring Credit Risks from the Authorised Person to another party through securitisation, provided that the conditions in Section 4.14 are met.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,5a4ad383-0e7b-476f-84ee-d6bce45b2270,9ae2763f-2e1a-4afb-ac8e-f57ce03a81c3,,,4.15.17,4.15.12,,,,,HV0066,ebd9610d5d4d47a7,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: e01e9f1e9dd5fd16,"If someone files a Supplementary Prospectus, when can the Regulator ask for an extra fee, and is that the same kind of situation where the Regulator can charge an extra fee for other filings or supervision work?","A Supplementary Prospectus filing does not automatically mean a fee must be paid. The Regulator can only ask for a supplementary fee if reviewing that Supplementary Prospectus will require the Regulator to incur substantial additional costs or to spend substantial additional effort in carrying out its review [#SRC:cec237a1-c364-4ed0-9197-dcac6160defb]. This is consistent with the wider permission for the Regulator to require a Person to pay a supplementary fee in situations where the Regulator expects substantial additional costs or substantial additional effort in dealing with regulatory matters such as an application, an authorisation, a filing, or on-going supervision [#TGT:64a0df5a-e946-4496-9fd3-244340c2a080]. In other words, the key trigger is not simply that a document was filed, but that the Regulator’s work on it is expected to be unusually resource-intensive. The Supplementary Prospectus example fits within the broader category of “filing” situations where extra cost or effort justifies an additional fee.","The filing of a Supplementary Prospectus does not trigger the payment of a fee unless the review of the Supplementary Prospectus will require the Regulator to incur substantial additional costs or expend substantial additional effort when conducting its review, in which event the Regulator may require payment of a supplementary fee in accordance with Rule 1.2.4.","Supplementary fees

The Regulator may require a Person to pay to the Regulator a supplementary fee in circumstances where it expects to incur substantial additional costs or expend substantial additional effort in dealing with an application, authorisation, filing or when conducting on-going supervision.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,cec237a1-c364-4ed0-9197-dcac6160defb,64a0df5a-e946-4496-9fd3-244340c2a080,,,9.3.1.Guidance,1.2.4,,,,,HV0067,e01e9f1e9dd5fd16,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

d350ec23b14294f4,"When an Exempt Fund can no longer satisfy the conditions needed to remain classified as an Exempt Fund, what must the Fund Manager do in relation to applying for the winding up of that Fund, and how does the availability of converting the Fund to a Qualified Investor Fund depend on whether the Fund meets the criteria for a Domestic Fund to be treated as a Qualified Investor Fund (including how its Units are offered and who may be Unitholders)?","If an Exempt Fund can no longer meet the relevant conditions required for it to remain classified as an Exempt Fund, the Fund Manager of that Fund is required to apply for the winding up of that Fund [#SRC:6e2b3cea-7166-4cff-a20a-f10f87ba8b03]. Instead of winding up, the Fund Manager may pursue an alternative regulatory outcome by changing the Fund’s classification, including converting the Fund to a Qualified Investor Fund, but only if the Fund meets the conditions applicable to a Qualified Investor Fund [#SRC:6e2b3cea-7166-4cff-a20a-f10f87ba8b03]. In assessing whether conversion to a Qualified Investor Fund is available for a Domestic Fund, the Fund Manager must ensure the Domestic Fund satisfies the defining criteria for being treated as a Qualified Investor Fund: its Units must be offered only by way of a private placement, and all its Unitholders must meet the criteria to be classified as Professional Clients [#TGT:edeb67fb-b685-4937-bc79-820dd671f855]. If those Domestic Fund criteria are not met, the Fund would not qualify on that basis as a Qualified Investor Fund, and the Fund Manager would need to proceed with the required winding-up application triggered by the loss of Exempt Fund conditions, or consider another permitted reclassification route [#SRC:6e2b3cea-7166-4cff-a20a-f10f87ba8b03].","If an Exempt Fund can no longer meet the relevant conditions set out in Rule ‎3.3.3 to be classified as an Exempt Fund, the Fund Manager of that Fund is required, under Section 112 of the FSMR, to apply for the winding up of that Fund. Alternatively, the Fund Manager may have that Fund moved to the classification of a Public Fund, which requires the satisfaction of the requirements and formalities specific to that type of Fund. An Exempt Fund may also, if it wishes to, convert to a Qualified Investor Fund provided it meets the conditions applicable to a Qualified Investor Fund in Rule ‎3.3.4.","A Domestic Fund is a Qualified Investor Fund, if:

column2: its Units are offered to persons only by way of a private placement;
all its Unitholders are persons who meet the criteria to be classified as Professional Clients; and

the initial subscription to be paid by a person to become a Unitholder is at least US$500,000.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,6e2b3cea-7166-4cff-a20a-f10f87ba8b03,edeb67fb-b685-4937-bc79-820dd671f855,,,PART 5.14.1.Guidance.1,PART 2.3.3.4.(1),,,,,HV0068,d350ec23b14294f4,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 46321a06af84dda3,"If Securities are being admitted to trading on a Recognised Investment Exchange, when does the prohibition not apply because the Securities are treated as Exempt Securities, and what kinds of Securities count as Exempt Securities under the Regulator’s prescribed list?","The prohibition does not apply to admitting Securities to trading on a Recognised Investment Exchange when the Securities being admitted are Exempt Securities, but this is not a blanket exclusion: the admission is still subject to the separate requirement that applies to this situation [#SRC:f70272ac-30bf-4e62-92d7-8b863f75cdf9]. To know whether the exclusion is available, you must check whether the Securities fit within one of the types the Regulator has prescribed as Exempt Securities [#TGT:16a48ee7-becd-40f8-8af0-17dbcd09dfc0]. Those types include, for example: small additional issuances of shares of the same class already admitted (measured over 12 months); replacement shares with no increase in issued capital; Securities linked to a takeover offer or merger where a document with information the Regulator regards as equivalent to a prospectus is available; rights issues or free/share-dividend issues where the Securities are the same class and an information document is made available; offers to directors, employees, or close relatives with the same-class and document conditions; shares created by conversion or exercise into the same class; and certain admissions from another market where trading history, ongoing compliance, and an English summary document approved by the Regulator are provided. If none of these definitions fits, the exclusion does not apply.","The prohibition in section 61(1) of the FSMR does not apply, subject to the requirement in Rule 4.4.2, to the admission to trading on a Recognised Investment Exchange of Securities that are Exempt Securities under Rule 4.4.1.","For the purposes of section 61(3)(b) of the FSMR the Regulator hereby prescribes the types of Securities that are Exempt Securities:

column2: Shares representing, over a period of 12 months, less than 10% of the number of Shares of the same class already admitted to trading on the same Recognised Investment Exchange;

Shares issued in substitution for Shares of the same class already admitted to trading on the same Recognised Investment Exchange, if the issue of the Shares does not involve any increase in the issued capital;
Securities offered in connection with a Takeover Offer, if a document is available containing information which is regarded by the Regulator as being equivalent to that of a Prospectus;

Securities offered, allotted or to be allotted in connection with a merger, if a document is available containing information which is regarded by the Regulator as being equivalent to that of the Prospectus;
Securities offered, allotted or to be allotted in connection with a rights issue if:
the Securities are of the same class as the Securities already admitted to trading on the same Recognised Investment Exchange; and
a document is made available containing information on the number and nature of the Securities and the reasons for and details of the Offer;

Shares offered, allotted or to be allotted to existing Shareholders free of charge, or in respect of dividends paid out in the form of Shares of the same class as the Shares in respect of which the dividends are paid, if:
the Shares are of the same class as the Shares already admitted to trading on the same Recognised Investment Exchange; and
a document is made available containing information on the number and nature of the Shares and the reasons for and details of the Offer;

Securities offered, allotted or to be allotted to an existing or former Director or Employee, or any Close Relative of such a Director or Employee, of the Issuer or a member of the same Group as the Issuer and if:
the Securities are of the same class as the Securities already admitted to trading on the same Recognised Investment Exchange; and
a document is made available containing information on the number and nature of the Securities and the reasons for and detail of the Offer;

Shares resulting from the conversion or exchange of other Securities or from the exercise of the rights conferred by other Securities, if the Shares are of the same class as the Shares already admitted to trading on the same Recognised Investment Exchange; or
Securities already admitted to trading on another Recognised Investment Exchange or Regulated Exchange (the ""Other Market""), where:
the Securities, or Securities of the same class, have been admitted to trading and continuously traded on the Other Market for more than 18 months;
the on-going obligations for trading on that Other Market have been complied with; and

the Person requesting the admission to trading of the Securities under this exemption makes a summary document in the English language which is approved by the Regulator in accordance with the requirements in section 4.6 and published:
containing the information set out in Rule 4.5.2(1)(b);
stating where the most recent and current Prospectus, if any, can be obtained; and
specifying where the financial information disclosed by the Issuer pursuant to its on-going disclosure obligations of the Other Market is available.

Securities offered in connection with any issue of Securities under Rules 9.7.1 or 9.7.4, where the Securities are of the same class already admitted to trading on the same Recognised Investment Exchange.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,f70272ac-30bf-4e62-92d7-8b863f75cdf9,16a48ee7-becd-40f8-8af0-17dbcd09dfc0,,,4.4.Guidance.2.,4.4.1,,,,,HV0069,46321a06af84dda3,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 7745e6835dca8da7,"When can a letter of credit count as a qualifying letter of credit that the Regulator may allow to be included as eligible capital, and what specific features must it have (like being enforceable in ADGM or an approved jurisdiction, not needing all-party consent to change, no collateral required from the Captive Insurer, and the bank’s rating and regulation)?","A letter of credit can be treated as a qualifying letter of credit only if it both meets the required conditions for the relevant requirements and the Regulator allows it to be included as eligible capital [#SRC:09531ba6-44f7-4113-bdf4-943582ecc05c]. Meeting the required conditions means the letter of credit must be unconditional and irrevocable, and it must not include a subordination clause [#TGT:27f296e6-bc33-466d-b0c3-d6ff38a741d3]. It must be legally enforceable in ADGM or in another jurisdiction that the Regulator has approved for this purpose, and it must not be capable of being cancelled or amended unless all parties consent [#TGT:27f296e6-bc33-466d-b0c3-d6ff38a741d3]. It also needs to be for a fixed amount and renewable annually [#TGT:27f296e6-bc33-466d-b0c3-d6ff38a741d3]. The agreement between the bank and the Captive Insurer must not require the Captive Insurer to give collateral to the bank as a condition for issuing the letter of credit [#TGT:27f296e6-bc33-466d-b0c3-d6ff38a741d3]. Finally, the bank providing it must be rated at least BBB+ by Standard & Poor’s (or an equivalent rating by another Approved Rating Agency) and be regulated in ADGM or another jurisdiction approved by the Regulator, at issue and afterwards [#TGT:27f296e6-bc33-466d-b0c3-d6ff38a741d3].","A letter of credit is a qualifying letter of credit if:

column2: it meets the requirements in Rule ‎3.1.4(2); and
the Regulator allows, under Rule 2(2)(a), that it be included as eligible capital.","A letter of credit meets the requirements of this Rule 3.1.4(2) if:
it is unconditional and irrevocable;
it does not contain a subordination clause;
it is legally enforceable in ADGM or any other jurisdiction approved for this purpose by the Regulator;
it cannot be cancelled or amended without the consent of all parties;
it is for a fixed amount;
it is renewable annually;
the terms of the agreement between the bank and the Captive Insurer do not require the Captive Insurer to give collateral to the bank for issuing the letter of credit; and
the bank that provides the letter of credit is, at the time of issue, and afterwards:
rated at least BBB+ by Standard & Poor's or the equivalent by another Approved Rating Agency; and

regulated in ADGM or any other jurisdiction approved for this purpose by the Regulator.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,09531ba6-44f7-4113-bdf4-943582ecc05c,27f296e6-bc33-466d-b0c3-d6ff38a741d3,,,3.1.4.(1),3.1.4.(2),,,,,HV0070,7745e6835dca8da7,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 8ff811107a4ee8b8,"Where investments are made using Musharaka or Mudaraba contracts with commodities as the underlying assets, how must an Authorised Person calculate its Commodities Risk Capital Requirement, including the required treatment of Trading Book and Non Trading Book commodity positions and the permitted calculation approaches?","Where investments are made using Musharaka or Mudaraba contracts with commodities as the underlying assets, an Authorised Person must calculate its Commodities Risk Capital Requirement in the manner required for commodity exposures [#SRC:bbd0d60b-0179-4756-8de1-848cacc7db4e]. In doing so, the calculation must cover commodity positions in both the Trading Book and the Non Trading Book, rather than being limited to one book only [#TGT:e93a335b-caf1-4776-842f-11bd1e28aefe]. The Authorised Person must then apply one of the specified calculation approaches: either use its internal Market Risk model, provided that model has been approved by the Regulator for the purpose of calculating the Commodities Risk Capital Requirement, or apply the prescribed rules set out for this calculation method [#TGT:e93a335b-caf1-4776-842f-11bd1e28aefe]. Accordingly, when the commodity exposure arises through Musharaka or Mudaraba structures, the firm must ensure it selects an allowed approach and applies it consistently to the relevant Trading Book and Non Trading Book commodity positions to arrive at the Commodities Risk Capital Requirement [#SRC:bbd0d60b-0179-4756-8de1-848cacc7db4e] [#TGT:e93a335b-caf1-4776-842f-11bd1e28aefe].","Market risk. Where investments are made using Musharaka or Mudaraba contracts with commodities as the underlying assets, an Authorised Person must calculate its Commodities Risk Capital Requirement in accordance with PRU Rule 5.7.1.","An Authorised Person in Category 1, 2 or 5 must calculate its Commodities Risk Capital Requirement in respect of Trading Book and Non Trading Book commodity positions by:

column2: applying its internal Market Risk model which has been approved by the Regulator for this purpose; or

applying the Rules set out in Section A6.5.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,bbd0d60b-0179-4756-8de1-848cacc7db4e,e93a335b-caf1-4776-842f-11bd1e28aefe,,,5.4.10,5.7.1,,,,,HV0071,8ff811107a4ee8b8,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 2b8ee19ae20c88cf,What must a Third Party Provider do to ensure its professional indemnity insurance both remains adequate to reimburse Customers if operational risk events occur and also stays above the required threshold tied to recent Third Party Transactions?,"A Third Party Provider must maintain professional indemnity insurance coverage that is sufficient in purpose and effect to reimburse Customers if operational risk events occur, meaning the coverage must be kept at a level that can respond to losses arising from such events and support customer reimbursement when needed [#SRC:c9a29acd-37bb-40cb-9516-3121dbf18b53]. In addition to that customer-protection objective, the Third Party Provider must continuously monitor its remaining professional indemnity insurance coverage and ensure it does not fall below a quantitative floor linked to its transaction activity: at all times, the remaining coverage must be greater than thirty times the average daily value of all Third Party Transactions over the past ninety calendar days [#TGT:aaaa3ad8-9dea-490e-bd62-04177ed8aa0b].
