Practically, this requires the Third Party Provider to track Third Party Transactions over the rolling ninety-day period, calculate the average daily value, apply the thirty-times multiplier, and compare the result to the remaining coverage so that coverage is maintained and adjusted as transaction volumes change, while still meeting the overarching requirement that coverage be sufficient to reimburse Customers following operational risk events [#SRC:c9a29acd-37bb-40cb-9516-3121dbf18b53] [#TGT:aaaa3ad8-9dea-490e-bd62-04177ed8aa0b].",Rule 6.12A.2 requires a Third Party Provider to maintain sufficient professional indemnity insurance coverage to reimburse Customers should operational risk events occur.,Transaction Limits. A Third Party Provider must ensure that its remaining professional indemnity insurance coverage is always greater than thirty times the average daily value of all Third Party Transactions in the past ninety calendar days.,SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,c9a29acd-37bb-40cb-9516-3121dbf18b53,aaaa3ad8-9dea-490e-bd62-04177ed8aa0b,,,6.12A.4.Guidance.2.,6.12A.2,,,,,HV0072,2b8ee19ae20c88cf,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

1e44cabdde5dba07,"When the Customer is not a Natural Person and the Customer and the Third Party Provider have agreed in writing to disapply the provisions governing withdrawal of consent, to what extent may the Customer still withdraw consent to a series of Third Party Transactions, and what is the authorisation status of previously consented but unexecuted Third Party Transactions at the time of withdrawal, taking into account the stated condition that applies to withdrawal?","If the Customer is not a Natural Person, the Customer and the Third Party Provider are permitted to agree in writing that the provisions dealing with withdrawal of consent do not apply [#SRC:10510c2c-99d3-4cba-bac5-61cda5d00d44]. Absent (or unless overridden by) such a written agreement, the Customer is permitted to withdraw consent to a series of Third Party Transactions at any time, but this permission operates subject to the stated condition that applies to withdrawal [#TGT:e4c92e77-6fe0-46b4-a71f-9f3a479ee273]. Where consent is withdrawn under that permission, any Third Party Transactions that were previously consented to but have not yet been executed at the time of withdrawal will no longer be regarded as authorised [#TGT:e4c92e77-6fe0-46b4-a71f-9f3a479ee273]. Accordingly, compliance should confirm (i) whether the Customer is not a Natural Person, and (ii) whether there is a written agreement between the Customer and the Third Party Provider disapplying the withdrawal-of-consent provisions; if so, the default ability to withdraw consent and the resulting change in authorisation status may not apply as described [#SRC:10510c2c-99d3-4cba-bac5-61cda5d00d44].","Where the Customer is not a Natural Person, the Customer and the Third Party Provider may agree in writing that the following Rules do not apply:

column2: Rules 20.2.15 and 20.2.16 (charges for information);
Rule 20.7.3 and 20.7.4 (withdrawal of consent);
Rule 20.8.2 (revocation of a Payment Order);
Rules 20.10.1 and 20.10.2 (requests for refund);
Rule 20.11.1 (evidence on authentication and execution);
Rule 20.12.5 (liability for charges); and

column1: the parties may agree that a different time period applies concerning unauthorised or incorrectly executed Payment Transactions for the purposes of Rule 20.10.1.","Subject to Rule 20.8.2, the Customer may withdraw consent to a series of Third Party Transactions at any time.  All Third Party Transactions which have been previously consented to but not yet executed at the time that consent has been withdrawn will no longer be regarded as authorised.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,10510c2c-99d3-4cba-bac5-61cda5d00d44,e4c92e77-6fe0-46b4-a71f-9f3a479ee273,,,20.4.1,20.7.4,,,,,HV0073,1e44cabdde5dba07,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

77032a5135185e5a,"If a Petroleum Reporting Entity is disclosing material Contingent Resources estimates for the first time, what must it say about the types of permits or licences it holds, and what other required explanations must it include about the data, the basis for the discovery, and how the estimates were made?","If a Petroleum Reporting Entity discloses material estimates of Contingent Resources that it has not previously disclosed, it must include the types of permits or licences it holds that relate to the estimates and are relevant to the disclosed Contingent Resources estimates [#SRC:a9ffc27d-5147-4066-826f-22c25cd1e704] [#TGT:cd78e857-9a44-49d6-932d-db3b31f20dec]. It must also explain the new data and information and explain how that new data and information affected the estimates (including Contingent Resources), and it must describe any changes or additions to information it previously disclosed that relates to Contingent Resources [#SRC:a9ffc27d-5147-4066-826f-22c25cd1e704]. Alongside those points, it must provide the basis for confirming a significant quantity of potentially moveable Petroleum and for determining that a discovery has been made, and it must describe the method used to estimate the Contingent Resources, the key contingencies that led to the Contingent Resources classification, and any further appraisal drilling and evaluation work that will be undertaken to assess commercial recovery and progress the project [#TGT:cd78e857-9a44-49d6-932d-db3b31f20dec]. If the estimates depend on technology under development or involve Unconventional Petroleum Resources, the disclosure must also include the additional specified explanations and details for those situations [#TGT:cd78e857-9a44-49d6-932d-db3b31f20dec].","A Petroleum Reporting Entity making a disclosure under Rule 12.6.1 must ensure the disclosure contains:

column2: the types of permits or licences held by the Petroleum Reporting Entity relating to the estimates;
an explanation of the new data and information;
an explanation of how the new data and information has affected the estimates of Prospective Resources, Contingent Resources or Petroleum Resources; and
any changes or additions to the information previously disclosed relating to:
Prospective Resources under Rules 12.8.1(1) to 12.8.1(4);
Contingent Resources under Rules 12.10.1(1) to 12.10.1(5); and

Petroleum Reserves under Rules 12.12.1(1) to 12.12.1(7).","A Petroleum Reporting Entity disclosing estimates of Contingent Resources that are material, and that have not previously been disclosed by the Petroleum Reporting Entity, must ensure the disclosure contains:
the types of permits or licences held by the Petroleum Reporting Entity relevant to the disclosed estimates of Contingent Resources;
the basis for, confirming the existence of a significant quantity of potentially moveable Petroleum, and the determination of a discovery;
a description of:
the method of estimation;
the key contingencies that resulted in the estimates being classified as Contingent Resources;
any further appraisal drilling and evaluation work to be undertaken to assess the potential for commercial recovery, and to progress the relevant project;

if the disclosed estimates of Contingent Resources are contingent on technology under development, to ensure that Unrecoverable quantities are not classified as part of the Contingent Resources, an explanation of whether the technology has:
been demonstrated to be commercially viable in analogous reservoirs;

been demonstrated to be commercially viable in other reservoirs that are not analogous, and that a pilot project, which is planned and budgeted, will be necessary to demonstrate commerciality for this reservoir; or

not been demonstrated to be commercially viable, but is currently under active development, and there is sufficient evidence to indicate that the technology may reasonably be expected to be available for commercial application within five years; and
if the disclosed estimates of Contingent Resources relate to Unconventional Petroleum Resources, the:
type(s) of Unconventional Contingent Resource;
land area;
number of wells; and

specialised extraction technology proposed to be utilised.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,a9ffc27d-5147-4066-826f-22c25cd1e704,cd78e857-9a44-49d6-932d-db3b31f20dec,,,12.6.2,12.10.1,,,,,HV0074,77032a5135185e5a,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,target_only_sufficient,

column1: 87231a712205b723,"When a Mining Reporting Entity makes a disclosure that includes forecast financial information derived from a Production Target and also discloses an estimate of Ore Reserves, what specific categories of information must it include about (i) the assumptions used to determine the forecast financial information and (ii) the key factors or assumptions underlying the Ore Reserves estimate?","Where a Mining Reporting Entity discloses forecast financial information derived from a Production Target, it must include comprehensive information about the assumptions used to determine that forecast financial information, including all material economic assumptions employed, any statement and methodological explanation if those material economic assumptions are considered commercially sensitive, and all other material assumptions utilised; it must also identify the Production Target from which the forecast financial information is derived (including the required information associated with that Production Target) [#SRC:2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489]. In addition, when the same Mining Reporting Entity discloses an estimate of Ore Reserves, the disclosure must also include key information relating to the factors or assumptions supporting that Ore Reserves estimate, specifically mining (recovery/dilution) factors or assumptions, metallurgical factors or assumptions, cut-off parameters, study status, and the relative accuracy/confidence of the estimate [#TGT:cb1ec09f-a7d3-4c38-ba2e-4e72ed8c3129]. Taken together, the disclosure package must therefore address both the forecast’s underlying economic and other material assumptions (and the Production Target basis) and the Ore Reserves estimate’s technical and study-related assumptions and confidence indicators, ensuring both elements are covered when they appear in the same disclosure.","A Mining Reporting Entity’s disclosure pursuant to Rule 11.9.1 must include:

column2: in relation to the assumptions used to determine the forecast financial information:
all material economic assumptions employed;

if the Mining Reporting Entity considers the material economic assumptions to be commercially sensitive, a statement to that effect and an explanation of the methodology used to determine the material economic assumptions; and

column1: A Mining Reporting Entity that considers certain information relating to the material economic assumptions to be commercially sensitive should refer to paragraphs 47-54 of the Guidance on Mining and paragraphs 127 and 128 of the Guidance on Continuous Disclosure.

column2: all other material assumptions utilised.

the Production Target from which the forecast financial information is derived (including all the information contained in Rule 11.8.3).","ORE RESERVES . Rule 11.6 also requires that when a Mining Reporting Entity discloses an estimate of Ore Reserves, the disclosure is also to include key information relating to mining (recovery/dilution) factors or assumptions, metallurgical factors or assumptions, cut-off parameters, study status and the relative accuracy/confidence.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,mixed_difficulty,2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489,cb1ec09f-a7d3-4c38-ba2e-4e72ed8c3129,,,11.9.2,53),,,,,HV0075,87231a712205b723,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 27b02d45aee84f3f,"If an Authorised Person is in Category 1, 2 or 5 and also manages a PSIA that is an Unrestricted PSIA, what must it not do regarding (1) Financial Group Large Exposures (including the Financial Group’s PSIAus) compared to the Group’s Tier 1 and (2) exposures to a Counterparty or related counterparty groups compared to its Capital Resources, depending on how the exposure is financed?","If the Authorised Person falls within Category 1, 2 or 5 and also is an Authorised Person Managing a PSIA that is an Unrestricted PSIA, it is prohibited from exceeding specific exposure limits under both sets of requirements. Under the Financial Group Large Exposure restriction, it must not incur any Financial Group Large Exposure, including the Financial Group’s PSIAus, that is more than 25% of its Group’s Tier 1; any exposure above that level is not permitted. [#SRC:daaa6de1-3ef9-4148-ae13-789a1bb8a600] Separately, when managing the Unrestricted PSIA, it must not have an Exposure to a Counterparty, Connected Counterparty, a group of Closely Related Counterparties, or a group of Connected Counterparties that exceeds the relevant percentage of its Capital Resources. The limit is 25% if the exposure is financed by its Capital Resources or Unrestricted PSIAs, and 40% if financed by an aggregate of its own Capital Resources and Unrestricted PSIAs. [#TGT:7521ffc6-250a-43ac-b7fd-68049d51519f] These prohibitions apply based on the stated counterparty groupings and financing basis.","Subject to IFR Rule 5.4.15, an Authorised Person in Category 1, 2 or 5 must not incur any Financial Group Large Exposure, including the Financial Group's PSIAus, that exceeds 25% of its Group's Tier 1.","Exposure limits. An Authorised Person Managing a PSIA, which is an Unrestricted PSIA, must not have an Exposure to a Counterparty, Connected Counterparty, group of Closely Related Counterparties or to a group of Connected Counterparties that exceeds any one of the following percentages of its Capital Resources:

column2: 25% if financed by its Capital Resources or Unrestricted PSIAs; or

40% if financed by an aggregate of its own Capital Resources and Unrestricted PSIAs.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,daaa6de1-3ef9-4148-ae13-789a1bb8a600,7521ffc6-250a-43ac-b7fd-68049d51519f,,,8.4.1,5.4.15,,,,,HV0076,27b02d45aee84f3f,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,some_copied_acceptable,both_needed,

column1: 610fd687cbc00576,"If an Authorised Person is an MTF or OTF for spot commodity activities, how much regulatory capital must it hold compared with what a Recognised Investment Exchange must hold, including any extra buffer the Regulator can change?","In the spot commodity activities context described, when the FSRA applies the regulatory capital requirements to an Authorised Person that is an MTF or OTF, the amount of regulatory capital to be held is measured against operational expenses and is equivalent to six months of those expenses [#SRC:59dfe046-0591-4dc2-a1d3-f4b1d56e6ee8]. A Recognised Investment Exchange must also hold capital based on operational expenses, starting with an amount equal to six months’ operational expenses [#TGT:1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96]. In addition, the Recognised Investment Exchange must hold a further buffer amount that can be up to another six months’ operational expenses, unless the Regulator directs otherwise [#TGT:1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96]. So, both obligations use six months of operational expenses as the baseline measure, but only the Recognised Investment Exchange requirement explicitly includes a possible extra buffer layer that may be adjusted by the Regulator. The practical effect is that the Recognised Investment Exchange capital requirement can extend beyond the six-month baseline depending on regulatory direction.","REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS - SPOT COMMODITY ACTIVITIES
The FSRA applies the regulatory capital requirements in COBS Rule 22.10 in two different scenarios, such that:

column2: where the Authorised Person is an MTF or OTF, the regulatory capital to be held (under COBS Rule 22.10.1(a) and MIR Rule 3.2.1) is equivalent to 6 months’ operational expenses ; and

in relation to all other Authorised Persons, the ‘conventional’ regulatory capital requirements applicable to the Regulated Activities undertaken apply.","A Recognised Investment Exchange shall hold the following capital:
an amount equal to 6 months' operational expenses; plus

unless the Regulator directs otherwise, an additional buffer amount of up to a further 6 months' operational expenses.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,59dfe046-0591-4dc2-a1d3-f4b1d56e6ee8,1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96,,,54),3.2.1,,,,,HV0077,610fd687cbc00576,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 048e236039d09c7e,"If the Regulator tells a Reporting Entity that a reporting requirement applies and how long it must follow it, when does the Reporting Entity have to fill out MKT Form 10-1 every quarter, and what else might the Regulator include in that notice?","The Reporting Entity has to complete MKT Form 10-1 on a quarterly basis when the Regulator makes the obligation apply through one of the listed triggers: the Regulator requires the form as a condition of admission to the Official List, the Regulator classifies the Reporting Entity as a Mining Exploration Reporting Entity or a Petroleum Exploration Reporting Entity, or the Regulator otherwise requires the form under the statutory basis referenced in the obligation. [#TGT:67e6fb61-6313-4d10-b3bb-b9b99d81cb75] Separately, when the Regulator applies the relevant reporting framework to the Reporting Entity, the Regulator will inform the Reporting Entity that it applies and will state the length of time the Reporting Entity is required to comply. [#SRC:6ad7b78f-3be1-497f-944b-9d2ddcef1e86] If it is relevant, the Regulator’s notice may also include any other requirement imposed on the Reporting Entity in relation to its obligations under that framework. Taken together, the quarterly form-filing duty depends on the Regulator’s action, and the notice clarifies both that the duty applies and the period and any additional requirements tied to it.","The Regulator, when applying Rule 10.1.3B(1), will inform the Reporting Entity that the Rule applies, the length of time the Reporting Entity is required to comply with the Rule and, if applicable, any other requirement imposed on the Reporting Entity in relation to its obligations under the Rule.","A Reporting Entity must complete MKT Form 10-1 on a quarterly basis if the Regulator:

column2: requires it as a condition of admission to the Official List pursuant to section 52(1)(b) of the FSMR;
classifies the Reporting Entity as a Mining Exploration Reporting Entity or a Petroleum Exploration Reporting Entity; or

requires it pursuant to section 84 of the FSMR.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,6ad7b78f-3be1-497f-944b-9d2ddcef1e86,67e6fb61-6313-4d10-b3bb-b9b99d81cb75,,,10.1.3B.(1).Guidance.3.,10.1.3B.(1),,,,,HV0078,048e236039d09c7e,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 713051124c871887,"If a Recognised Clearing House cannot get one specific transaction settled, can it still be treated as meeting the Recognition Requirement, and what must its required satisfactory arrangements include by way of referencing other requirements?","Yes. A Recognised Clearing House is permitted to rely on the position that it will not be regarded as failing to comply with the Recognition Requirement just because it is unable to arrange for a specific transaction to be settled [#TGT:a15123d3-b822-401d-9551-e8759dd9e84e]. However, that does not remove the need for it to have the required satisfactory arrangements in place. Those satisfactory arrangements should include a reference to the requirements that are identified as the relevant set to be pointed to, so that the arrangements are tied back to those requirements rather than standing alone [#SRC:549c69d5-2c89-4747-8878-9ae4ce57346e]. Put simply, the “not treated as failing” point is a narrow protection for a single settlement problem, while the arrangements obligation is about having an overall framework that is documented and that directs the reader to the referenced requirements. The Recognised Clearing House should therefore keep its arrangements current and ensure they contain the required reference, even when it needs to rely on the protection for an individual transaction that cannot be settled.",The satisfactory arrangements required by Rule 3.8.1 should reference the requirements set out in Rule 4.3.3.,A Recognised Clearing House will not be regarded as failing to comply with the Recognition Requirement merely because it is unable to arrange for a specific transaction to be settled.,SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,549c69d5-2c89-4747-8878-9ae4ce57346e,a15123d3-b822-401d-9551-e8759dd9e84e,,,3.8.3.Guidance.1.,4.3.3,,,,,HV0079,713051124c871887,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

57e9094f0c23a7a5,"When an Authorised Person determines its Credit RWA as a sum of RWAs across exposure categories, what must it include and exclude when calculating the RWA component for its Credit Risk Exposures, so that this CR Exposures component is correctly separated from securitisation Exposures and other non-credit-risk items?","An Authorised Person’s Credit RWA is determined by summing distinct RWA components, including the RWA for all its Credit Risk Exposures (CR Exposures), the RWA for all its securitisation Exposures (SE Exposures), and the RWA for its Counterparty Risk Exposures [#SRC:5e5b0814-b3c0-441d-b92e-c7fe290a8020]. To ensure the CR Exposures component is calculated on the correct scope before it is added into that overall sum, the Authorised Person must include, within its calculation of RWA for CR Exposures, any on balance sheet asset and any off balance sheet item [#TGT:cb5e6ab2-3cae-450b-87c6-acb11128d3f0]. At the same time, it must exclude from the CR Exposures calculation any SE Exposure, any securitised Exposure that meets the requirements for recognition of risk transference in a Traditional Securitisation, and any Exposure classified as a position or instrument in the Trading Book [#TGT:cb5e6ab2-3cae-450b-87c6-acb11128d3f0]. This separation ensures securitisation-related exposures are not double-counted within the CR Exposures component when computing total Credit RWA [#SRC:5e5b0814-b3c0-441d-b92e-c7fe290a8020].","The Credit RWA of an Authorised Person is the sum of:

column2: its risk weighted assets (RWA) for all its Credit Risk Exposures (referred to in these Rules as ""CR Exposures"") calculated in accordance with Rules 4.8.2 and 4.8.3;
its RWA for all its securitisation Exposures (referred to in these Rules as ""SE Exposures"") calculated in accordance with Rule 4.8.4 and Section 4.14; and

its RWA for its Counterparty Risk Exposures as calculated in accordance with Sections A4.6 to A4.8.","Calculation of RWA for Credit Risk Exposures (CR Exposures). An Authorised Person must include in its calculation of RWA for CR Exposures:
any on balance sheet asset; and
any off balance sheet item; but excluding:
any SE Exposure;
any securitised Exposure that meets the requirements for the recognition of risk transference in a Traditional Securitisation set out in Section 4.14; and

any Exposure classified as a position or instrument in the Trading Book in accordance with Section A2.1.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,5e5b0814-b3c0-441d-b92e-c7fe290a8020,cb5e6ab2-3cae-450b-87c6-acb11128d3f0,,,4.8.1.(2),4.8.2,,,,,HV0080,57e9094f0c23a7a5,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 229b60d52a727226,"When an Authorised Person engaged in regulated activities in relation to Virtual Assets is required to hold regulatory capital in a manner consistent with the requirements applicable to a Recognised Investment Exchange, what form must that regulatory capital take, and what minimum capital amounts must a Recognised Investment Exchange hold (including any buffer that may be varied by the Regulator)?","An Authorised Person engaged in regulated activities in relation to Virtual Assets is required to hold regulatory capital in a way that aligns with the requirements applicable to a Recognised Investment Exchange, and—under those aligned requirements—the Authorised Person’s regulatory capital must be held in fiat form [#SRC:9795daec-7cae-4276-a676-296830fc723d]. In parallel, the Recognised Investment Exchange itself has a specific capital holding obligation: it shall hold capital equal to 6 months’ operational expenses, and, unless the Regulator directs otherwise, it must also hold an additional buffer amount of up to a further 6 months’ operational expenses [#TGT:1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96]. Read together, the cross-referenced framework means the Authorised Person’s capital must satisfy the fiat-form constraint while being calibrated by reference to the Recognised Investment Exchange-style expense-based capital baseline and the potential additional buffer, with the buffer’s application and extent subject to direction by the Regulator [#SRC:9795daec-7cae-4276-a676-296830fc723d] [#TGT:1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96].","REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR AUTHORISED PERSONS ENGAGED IN REGULATED ACTIVITIES IN RELATION TO VIRTUAL ASSETS

Given the nature of, and the risks associated with Virtual Assets, COBS Rule 17.3 requires an Authorised Person to hold regulatory capital in a manner consistent with MIR Rule 3.2.1 (being the requirements that a Recognised Investment Exchange must meet). Pursuant to these Rules, regulatory capital held by an Authorised Person must be in fiat form.","A Recognised Investment Exchange shall hold the following capital:

column2: an amount equal to 6 months' operational expenses; plus

unless the Regulator directs otherwise, an additional buffer amount of up to a further 6 months' operational expenses.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,9795daec-7cae-4276-a676-296830fc723d,1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96,,,31),3.2.1,,,,,HV0081,229b60d52a727226,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 80d6c95ebae92dd0,"When an Authorised Person is required to retain records of voice or electronic communications for at least two years, how should it determine whether particular communications fall outside the scope because they are general market-condition discussions not intended to lead to a specific Transaction, or because they occur between Fund Managers (or between Fund Managers and Eligible Custodians) of the same Fund acting in that capacity?","An Authorised Person must retain all records of voice or electronic communication for a minimum of two years, and this sits alongside related recordkeeping expectations such as being able to demonstrate prompt accessibility, keeping records in a comprehensible form (or being able to reproduce them promptly), and implementing procedures to prevent unauthorised alteration [#SRC:1dc324af-ed0d-41c9-9593-a65d39f6eb80]. In applying that retention requirement, the Authorised Person should also assess whether the communications in question fall within categories described as outside the scope of a related obligation, including (a) communications between Fund Managers, or between Fund Managers and Eligible Custodians of the same Fund when acting in that capacity, and (b) voice and electronic communications that are not intended to lead to the conclusion of a specific Transaction and instead are general conversations about market conditions [#TGT:7b6f7ff4-f87f-4553-8897-071620379a1f]. Practically, this means the Authorised Person should classify communications by purpose and participants (e.g., transaction-intent versus general market discussion; intra-fund operational communications versus other interactions) and ensure its procedures and record formats support prompt retrieval and integrity for the communications it must retain.","To comply with Rule 6.8.1‎(b), an Authorised Person must:

column2: be able to demonstrate prompt accessibility of all records;
maintain records in comprehensible form or must be capable of being promptly so reproduced;
make and implement appropriate procedures to prevent unauthorised alteration of its records; and
retain all records of voice or electronic communication for a minimum of two years.","The obligation in Rule ‎6.8.1(a) does not apply to the following:
Corporate Finance Business;
corporate treasury functions;
communications between Fund Managers, or between Fund Managers and Eligible Custodians of the same Fund (when acting in that capacity); and

voice and electronic communications which are not intended to lead to the conclusion of a specific Transaction and are general conversations or communications about market conditions.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,1dc324af-ed0d-41c9-9593-a65d39f6eb80,7b6f7ff4-f87f-4553-8897-071620379a1f,,,6.8.1.(c),6.8.1.(b),,,,,HV0082,80d6c95ebae92dd0,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: df992550123bafca,"For a Remote Body’s annual report to the Regulator, what time period should the report cover, and how do you set the start and end dates so the period follows on correctly from the last report (or, if there was no last report, from the Recognition Order), especially if the Remote Body changes its reporting period?","The Remote Body must give the Regulator an annual report, and the period covered by that report should most conveniently be one year [#SRC:1bdaf884-5e47-444f-a4b8-9cedd8d6e757], but it still has to be defined using the required start/end rules and continuity expectations [#TGT:dfcc4e9a-d1ad-454a-9f55-22de40772814]. To set the period, start counting from the day after the period covered by the last report. If there is no earlier report, start after the making of the Recognition Order recognising the Remote Body as such. The period then ends on the date you specify in the report; if you do not specify an end date, it ends on the date of the report itself. If the Remote Body decides to change the reporting period (for example, to align with a different cycle), it should keep the periods continuous by making the first day of the new period the day immediately after the last day of the previous period. Copies of the report should then be sent to the Regulator within two months after the period ends.",The period covered by the report to be submitted under Rule 7.4.1 would most conveniently be one year.,"A Remote Body shall provide the Regulator with an annual report which contains the information set out in Rule ‎7.4.2. In relation to the report:

column2: the period covered by such a report starts on the day after the period covered by its last report or, if there is no such report, after the making of the Recognition Order recognising the Remote Body as such, and ends on the date specified in the report or, if no date is specified, on the date of the report.

if a Remote Body changes the period covered by its report, it should ensure that the first day of the period covered by a report is the day immediately following the last day of the period covered by the previous report.

copies of the report should be sent to the Regulator within two months after the end of the period to which it relates.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,1bdaf884-5e47-444f-a4b8-9cedd8d6e757,dfcc4e9a-d1ad-454a-9f55-22de40772814,,,7.4.1.Guidance,7.4.1,,,,,HV0083,df992550123bafca,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 4fda40b2c8db34fa,"Where the Customer is not a Natural Person and the Customer and the Third Party Provider agree in writing to apply a different notification time period for unauthorised or incorrectly executed Payment Transactions, what must the Customer do to remain entitled to redress for an unauthorised or incorrectly executed Third Party Transaction, and how does that agreed time period interact with the default deadline?","When the Customer is not a Natural Person, the Customer and the Third Party Provider are permitted to agree in writing that a different time period applies for unauthorised or incorrectly executed Payment Transactions for the relevant refund/redress framework [#SRC:10510c2c-99d3-4cba-bac5-61cda5d00d44]. Even where such an agreed time period is in place, the Customer’s entitlement to redress remains conditional on notification to its Third Party Provider without undue delay once the Customer becomes aware of an unauthorised or incorrectly executed Third Party Transaction [#TGT:d299e513-87d9-47de-9c0f-1f15cca91cbb]. Absent an agreed alternative, the default outer limit is that the Customer must notify the Third Party Provider no later than twelve months after the date of execution to be entitled to redress [#TGT:d299e513-87d9-47de-9c0f-1f15cca91cbb]. Accordingly, the compliance approach is: confirm whether the Customer is not a Natural Person; verify there is a written agreement with the Third Party Provider setting a different time period; and ensure the Customer’s notification is made without undue delay and within the applicable time period (the agreed period if validly set, otherwise the twelve-month limit) [#SRC:10510c2c-99d3-4cba-bac5-61cda5d00d44] [#TGT:d299e513-87d9-47de-9c0f-1f15cca91cbb].","Where the Customer is not a Natural Person, the Customer and the Third Party Provider may agree in writing that the following Rules do not apply:

column2: Rules 20.2.15 and 20.2.16 (charges for information);
Rule 20.7.3 and 20.7.4 (withdrawal of consent);
Rule 20.8.2 (revocation of a Payment Order);
Rules 20.10.1 and 20.10.2 (requests for refund);
Rule 20.11.1 (evidence on authentication and execution);
Rule 20.12.5 (liability for charges); and

column1: the parties may agree that a different time period applies concerning unauthorised or incorrectly executed Payment Transactions for the purposes of Rule 20.10.1.","Subject to Rule 20.10.2, a Customer is only entitled to redress if it notifies its Third Party Provider without undue delay, and in any event no later than twelve months after the date of execution, on becoming aware of any unauthorised or incorrectly executed Third Party Transaction.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,10510c2c-99d3-4cba-bac5-61cda5d00d44,d299e513-87d9-47de-9c0f-1f15cca91cbb,,,20.4.1,20.10.1,,,,,HV0084,4fda40b2c8db34fa,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

ba828e11e8e65613,"If a Recognised Investment Exchange admits to trading a Financial Instrument that uses a benchmark or index from a Price Reporting Agency, what checks must the exchange do to make sure the agency meets the required standards for how it sets prices and handles transparency, governance, conflicts, and complaints?","If a Recognised Investment Exchange admits to trading a Financial Instrument that references an underlying benchmark or index provided by a Price Reporting Agency, the exchange must carry out appropriate due diligence to ensure the Price Reporting Agency meets the applicable requirements [#SRC:69082061-a103-4087-acae-fa41e87fd0da]. Those checks should be designed to confirm, at a minimum, that the Price Reporting Agency has fair and non-discriminatory procedures for establishing prices and that those procedures are made public; and that it can demonstrate adequate and appropriate transparency over its methodology, calculation and inputs so users can understand how the benchmark or index is derived and what its potential limitations are [#TGT:8a81e6cb-f1f1-4988-af97-f966f288017a]. Where appropriate, the exchange should also verify that the agency gives priority to concluded transactions and has measures to minimise selective reporting. In addition, due diligence should cover whether the agency is of good standing and repute as an independent and objective provider, has a sound corporate governance framework, has adequate arrangements to avoid staff conflicts of interest that could materially and adversely affect the price establishment process, and has adequate mechanisms to resolve complaints about its assessment process and methodology [#TGT:8a81e6cb-f1f1-4988-af97-f966f288017a].","When admitting to trading a Financial Instrument that references an underlying benchmark or index provided by a Price Reporting Agency, a Recognised Investment Exchange must undertake appropriate due diligence to ensure that the Price Reporting Agency meets the requirements in Rule 3.11.2.","For the purposes of Rules 3.11.1 and 3.11.3, a Price Reporting Agency must:

column2: have fair and non-discriminatory procedures for establishing prices of a Financial Instrument, which are made public;
demonstrate adequate and appropriate transparency over the methodology, calculation and inputs to allow users to understand how the benchmark or index is derived and its potential limitations;
where appropriate, give priority to concluded transactions in making assessments and adopt measures to minimise selective reporting;
be of good standing and repute as an independent and objective price reporting agency or index provider;
have a sound corporate governance framework;
have adequate arrangements to avoid its staff having any conflicts of interest where such conflicts are, or are likely to have, a material adverse impact on a price establishment process; and

adequate complaint resolution mechanisms to resolve any complaints about its assessment process and methodology.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,69082061-a103-4087-acae-fa41e87fd0da,8a81e6cb-f1f1-4988-af97-f966f288017a,,,3.11.1,3.11.2,,,,,HV0085,ba828e11e8e65613,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 5240ab88a5aa38dc,"When an initial annual fee becomes due partway through a calendar year and must be paid to the Regulator within the required timeframe, how must the prorated portion for the remainder of that calendar year be calculated based on the number of months remaining, and what payment timing applies?","Where an annual fee first becomes due during a calendar year, the initial annual fee must be paid in full to the Regulator within twenty days from the date it becomes due, but only after applying a proration for the remainder of that calendar year. The proration is not discretionary: the portion due of the annual designation fee must be determined by reference to the number of months remaining until the end of the calendar year, so the amount payable reflects the remaining months rather than a full-year charge. Accordingly, the compliance steps are (i) identify the date the fee becomes due, (ii) calculate the portion due by counting the months remaining to the end of the calendar year and basing the annual designation fee portion on that remaining-months figure, and then (iii) ensure the resulting prorated initial annual fee is paid in full to the Regulator within the twenty-day deadline. This approach applies to the initial annual fee proration for the remainder of the calendar year [#TGT:b8f50488-8fd2-4f32-a6c6-d841b3c60c37] and specifies the method for determining the portion due based on months remaining [#SRC:94b3f85d-c033-41a3-a884-c873899c049f].","In accordance with Rule 1.2.2, for Rule 10.2.1(a) the portion due of the annual designation fee is to be based on the number of months remaining until the end of the calendar year.","In regard to fees payable on an annual basis pursuant to these Rules:

column2: the initial annual fee must be paid in full to the Regulator within twenty days of the date on which the fee becomes due, prorated for the remainder of the calendar year; and

subsequent annual fees for the period commencing 1 January are payable in advance and must be paid in full to the Regulator on or before 31 January of the calendar year to which the fee relates.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,94b3f85d-c033-41a3-a884-c873899c049f,b8f50488-8fd2-4f32-a6c6-d841b3c60c37,,,10.2.1.Guidance,1.2.2,,,,,HV0086,5240ab88a5aa38dc,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 4b1efc25dc9528d2,"If a Mining Reporting Entity publishes a disclosure that includes Exploration Targets, Exploration Results, or estimates of Mineral Resources or Ore Reserves, what details must it say about the Competent Person(s), and what written approval must it get from the Competent Person(s) before publishing?","If a Mining Reporting Entity makes a disclosure that contains Exploration Targets, Exploration Results, or estimates of Mineral Resources or Ore Reserves, it must include specific information about the Competent Person(s) behind the disclosure. The disclosure must say that it is based on, and fairly represents, information and supporting documentation prepared by a named Competent Person(s). It must also explain, for each Competent Person, whether they are an employee of the Mining Reporting Entity or a Related Party; if they are not, the disclosure must name the Competent Person’s employer. In addition, the disclosure must identify the professional organisation of which each Competent Person is a member [#SRC:1133d38f-067b-4a0a-b325-b5c7b2512203]. Separately, before the disclosure is made, the Mining Reporting Entity must obtain the prior written consent of the Competent Person(s) covering the form and context in which the Exploration Results or the estimates (as relevant) and the supporting information are presented in the disclosure [#TGT:c30b96f6-edff-4774-b206-68a20fe00ba8].","Competent Persons . Subject to Rule 11.12.2, a disclosure by a Mining Reporting Entity containing Exploration Targets, Exploration Results, or estimates of Mineral Resources or Ore Reserves must state:

column2: that it is based on, and fairly represents, information and supporting documentation prepared by a named Competent Person(s);
in each case, whether the Competent Person is an employee of the Mining Reporting Entity or a Related Party and, if not, the name of the Competent Person’s employer; and

in each case, the name of the professional organisation of which each Competent Person is a member.","Competent Persons . The disclosure made in Rule 11.12.1 must only be made with the prior written consent of the Competent Person(s) as to the form and context in which the Exploration Results or estimates of Mineral Resources or Ore Reserves, as the case may be, and the supporting information is presented in the disclosure.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,1133d38f-067b-4a0a-b325-b5c7b2512203,c30b96f6-edff-4774-b206-68a20fe00ba8,,,11.12.1,11.12.2,,,,,HV0087,4b1efc25dc9528d2,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: eebe235602d9d4f8,"What arrangements must a Recognised Investment Exchange maintain to regularly reassess whether a Price Reporting Agency continues to satisfy the required standards for price establishment, transparency, governance, conflicts management, and complaint handling?","A Recognised Investment Exchange must maintain arrangements that ensure it regularly reviews, on an ongoing basis, whether a Price Reporting Agency continues to meet the applicable requirements, rather than relying on a one-time assessment at onboarding [#SRC:7728ff1d-b279-4806-b3fd-13f3e8a34e79]. In conducting that regular review, the Recognised Investment Exchange should assess whether the Price Reporting Agency continues to: operate fair and non-discriminatory, publicly available procedures for establishing prices of a Financial Instrument; provide adequate transparency over its methodology, calculations, and inputs so users can understand how any benchmark or index is derived and its limitations; and, where appropriate, prioritise concluded transactions and minimise selective reporting [#TGT:8a81e6cb-f1f1-4988-af97-f966f288017a]. The review should also cover whether the Price Reporting Agency remains of good standing and repute as an independent and objective provider, maintains a sound corporate governance framework, has adequate arrangements to avoid staff conflicts of interest that could materially adversely affect the price establishment process, and maintains adequate complaint resolution mechanisms for complaints about its assessment process and methodology [#TGT:8a81e6cb-f1f1-4988-af97-f966f288017a].",A Recognised Investment Exchange must have arrangements in place to regularly review whether a Price Reporting Agency continues to meet the requirements of Rule 3.11.2.,"For the purposes of Rules 3.11.1 and 3.11.3, a Price Reporting Agency must:

column2: have fair and non-discriminatory procedures for establishing prices of a Financial Instrument, which are made public;
demonstrate adequate and appropriate transparency over the methodology, calculation and inputs to allow users to understand how the benchmark or index is derived and its potential limitations;
where appropriate, give priority to concluded transactions in making assessments and adopt measures to minimise selective reporting;
be of good standing and repute as an independent and objective price reporting agency or index provider;
have a sound corporate governance framework;
have adequate arrangements to avoid its staff having any conflicts of interest where such conflicts are, or are likely to have, a material adverse impact on a price establishment process; and

adequate complaint resolution mechanisms to resolve any complaints about its assessment process and methodology.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,7728ff1d-b279-4806-b3fd-13f3e8a34e79,8a81e6cb-f1f1-4988-af97-f966f288017a,,,3.11.3,3.11.2,,,,,HV0088,eebe235602d9d4f8,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: f8720b938d34456e,"When an Authorised Person is considering whether it may recognise the effects of CRM from a Credit Derivative because the protection provider is an MDB, what must it do for any CR Exposure to those qualifying MDBs in terms of risk weighting, and which MDBs qualify for that treatment?","An Authorised Person may recognise the effects of CRM of a Credit Derivative only where the credit protection is provided by an eligible entity, including an MDB that falls within the relevant MDB category [#SRC:089417ca-c77d-4879-bc10-8d8138b1853b]. Where the counterparty/exposure is to a qualifying MDB within the Multilateral development bank (MDB) asset class, the Authorised Person must apply a 0% risk weight to any CR Exposure to those qualifying MDBs [#TGT:aed2a764-3ad1-4646-bf24-f6416556ffb4]. The qualifying MDBs for this 0% risk weight treatment are: the World Bank Group (International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), and International Finance Corporation (IFC)); the Asian Development Bank (ADB); the African Development Bank (AfDB); the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD); the Inter American Development Bank (IADB); the European Investment Bank (EIB); the European Investment Fund (EIF); the Nordic Investment Bank (NIB); the Caribbean Development Bank (CDB); the Islamic Development Bank (IDB); and the Council of Europe Development Bank (CEDB) [#TGT:aed2a764-3ad1-4646-bf24-f6416556ffb4].","An Authorised Person may recognise the effects of CRM of a Credit Derivative only if it is provided by any of the following entities:

column2: central government or central bank;
MDB referred to in Rules 4.12.7 to 4.12.9;
International Organisations referred to in Rule 4.12.9;
PSE;
banks and Securities firms which qualify for inclusion in bank asset class; or

any other entity that has an external credit assessment from a recognised credit rating agency that maps to a Credit Quality Grade 3 or better.","Multilateral development bank (MDB) asset class. An Authorised Person must apply a 0% risk weight to any CR Exposure to the qualifying MDBs set out below:

The World Bank Group comprised of the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA), and the International Finance Corporation (IFC);
The Asian Development Bank (ADB);
The African Development Bank (AfDB);
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD);
The Inter American Development Bank (IADB);
The European Investment Bank (EIB);
The European Investment Fund (EIF);
The Nordic Investment Bank (NIB);
The Caribbean Development Bank (CDB);
The Islamic Development Bank (IDB); and

The Council of Europe Development Bank (CEDB).",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,089417ca-c77d-4879-bc10-8d8138b1853b,aed2a764-3ad1-4646-bf24-f6416556ffb4,,,4.13.11.(1),4.12.8,,,,,HV0089,f8720b938d34456e,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 1b895eb922148ad3,"If an Authorised Person says its dealing is limited to acting only as Matched Principal, what category treatment applies to that limited dealing, and what does it have to do in practice to qualify as dealing in investments as a Matched Principal?","If an Authorised Person’s dealing activities are limited to acting only as Matched Principal, those dealing activities are treated as falling within the scope of the category identified for firms whose dealing is limited in that way [#SRC:e705fde9-d397-4a9f-b5a0-471529529c66]. To qualify, the Authorised Person must meet the definition of dealing in investments as a Matched Principal: it must enter into transactions as a principal only to fulfil its Clients’ orders, and it may hold positions for its own account only when it fails to match Clients’ orders [#TGT:36237c4c-0aef-4cdf-879a-4f72f0c1facc]. It also must keep the total market value of those positions at no more than 15% of the Firm’s Tier 1 Capital Resources, and ensure the positions are incidental and held only for the time reasonably required to carry out that type of transaction [#TGT:36237c4c-0aef-4cdf-879a-4f72f0c1facc]. Meeting these conditions supports the conclusion that the firm is acting only as Matched Principal for the purpose of applying the category scope described for such limited dealing [#SRC:e705fde9-d397-4a9f-b5a0-471529529c66].","Category 1
An Authorised Person is in Category 1 if:

column4: its Financial Services Permission authorises it to carry on one or more of the Regulated Activities of Accepting Deposits or Managing a Profit Sharing Investment Account which is a PSIAu; and
it does not meet the criteria of Category 5.

column1: A Category 1 Authorised Person may be authorised to conduct other Regulated Activities, but it is the authorisation for Accepting Deposits or Managing a Profit Sharing Investment Account which is a PSIAu that is determinative of its belonging to Category 1.

column2: A Category 2 Authorised Person may be authorised to conduct other Regulated Activities, but it is the authorisation for Dealing in Investments as Principal (not only as a Matched Principal) or Providing Credit, and the absence of authorisation for the activities specified in Rule 1.3.1, that are determinative of its belonging to Category 2.

Where the dealing activities of a firm are limited to acting only as Matched Principal, the activities fall in the scope of Category 3A in accordance with Rule 1.3.3(1). A definition of ""Matched Principal"" is in Rule 1.3.3(2).","For the purposes of these Rules, an Authorised Person Deals in Investments as a ""Matched Principal"" if:
it enters into transactions as a principal only for the purpose of fulfilling its Clients' orders;
it holds positions for its own account (""positions"") only as a result of a failure to match Clients' orders;
the total market value of the positions it holds is no more than 15% of the Firm's Tier 1 Capital Resources; and

the positions are incidental in nature and are strictly limited to the time reasonably required to carry out a transaction of that nature.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,e705fde9-d397-4a9f-b5a0-471529529c66,36237c4c-0aef-4cdf-879a-4f72f0c1facc,,,1.3.1,1.3.3.(2),,,,,HV0090,1b895eb922148ad3,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: e8d436b85bd1818e,"When a Mining Reporting Entity prepares a disclosure that includes forecast financial information derived from a Production Target and also includes ore reserves information supported by a separate report, what must the Mining Reporting Entity include about the assumptions used to determine the forecast financial information, and how must the ore reserves information in the disclosure be presented relative to the separate report and annexure?","Where a Mining Reporting Entity makes a disclosure that contains forecast financial information derived from a Production Target, it must include detailed information about the assumptions used to determine that forecast financial information: all material economic assumptions employed; if it considers those material economic assumptions commercially sensitive, it must state that and explain the methodology used to determine them; and it must also include all other material assumptions utilised [#SRC:2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489]. In addition, it must include the Production Target from which the forecast financial information is derived, together with the required accompanying information for that Production Target [#SRC:2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489]. For ore reserves information, the information included in the disclosure must be a fair and balanced representation of the information contained in a separate report, and that separate report must be included as an annexure to the disclosure [#TGT:b8cb4fdb-f627-43ae-90bf-801a549f8d63]. In complying, the FSRA does not expect a summary of all information in the separate report; instead, only information material to understanding the estimates of Mineral Resources in the separate report, and not otherwise included in the body of the disclosure, is expected to be included [#TGT:b8cb4fdb-f627-43ae-90bf-801a549f8d63].","A Mining Reporting Entity’s disclosure pursuant to Rule 11.9.1 must include:

column2: in relation to the assumptions used to determine the forecast financial information:
all material economic assumptions employed;

if the Mining Reporting Entity considers the material economic assumptions to be commercially sensitive, a statement to that effect and an explanation of the methodology used to determine the material economic assumptions; and

column1: A Mining Reporting Entity that considers certain information relating to the material economic assumptions to be commercially sensitive should refer to paragraphs 47-54 of the Guidance on Mining and paragraphs 127 and 128 of the Guidance on Continuous Disclosure.

column2: all other material assumptions utilised.

the Production Target from which the forecast financial information is derived (including all the information contained in Rule 11.8.3).","ORE RESERVES . Pursuant to Rule 11.6.1, the information included in the disclosure must be a fair and balanced representation of the information contained in the separate report prepared in accordance with Rule 11.6.2 (which must be included as an annexure to the disclosure).  In complying with this obligation, the FSRA does not expect a Mining Reporting Entity to prepare a summary of all the information contained in the separate report.  Instead, it is expected that that only information which is material to understanding the estimates of Mineral Resources contained in the separate report, that is not otherwise included in the body of the disclosure, be included.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,2c78a258-d9f2-4150-9d2c-ba681d8f9489,b8cb4fdb-f627-43ae-90bf-801a549f8d63,,,11.9.2,48),,,,,HV0091,e8d436b85bd1818e,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 58ca7134acbd61e8,"For the purposes of an investigation, when is the Investigator permitted to compel attendance at an interview and require answers to questions, and what procedural step must the Investigator take when directing the Person Under Investigation or any other person (whether or not connected to the Person Under Investigation) to attend at a specified time and place?","The Investigator is permitted, for the purposes of an investigation, to require a person (the interviewee) to attend an interview and answer questions [#SRC:a8953086-147f-4fb9-9370-ff7349385aaf]. Where the person being directed is the Person Under Investigation or any other person (whether or not connected to the Person Under Investigation), the Investigator may exercise this power by issuing a written notice that requires the person to attend an interview at a specified time and place and answer questions [#TGT:ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046]. Read together, this means the interview requirement is tied to the investigative purpose and can be imposed on both the Person Under Investigation and third parties, including those with no connection to the Person Under Investigation, provided the direction is communicated through written notice and specifies the time and place for the interview [#SRC:a8953086-147f-4fb9-9370-ff7349385aaf] [#TGT:ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046].","Power to require a person to attend an interview . Under section 206(1)(a) of FSMR, the Investigator has the power to require a person (the interviewee) to attend an interview and answer questions for the purposes of an investigation.","The Investigator may, by written notice, require the person who is the Person Under Investigation or any other person (whether or not connected to the Person Under Investigation) to—

column2: attend an interview at a Specified time and place and answer questions;
produce at a Specified time and place any Specified Documents or Documents of a Specified description;
provide such information as the Investigator may require;
provide such assistance as the Investigator may require; or

permit the Investigator to enter the business premises of such person during normal business hours for the purpose of inspecting and copying Documents on such premises.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,a8953086-147f-4fb9-9370-ff7349385aaf,ba9deea1-694d-4225-bf79-201773a12046,,,6.6.1,Part 17.206.(1),,,,,HV0092,58ca7134acbd61e8,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: cf8dd636cd9dd2cb,"When an Authorised Person wants to treat the netting of an on balance sheet Exposure against an offsetting on balance sheet item as eligible, what conditions must it satisfy regarding the netting agreement and its legal enforceability and documentation, and what additional prerequisite must be met before it may recognise that netting as eligible?","An Authorised Person may recognise as eligible the netting of an on balance sheet Exposure against an offsetting on balance sheet item only where the related Netting agreement meets the specified condition that governs eligibility [#SRC:6446b9df-ac01-4d04-bb14-029e92f0b3f7]. In addition, for the Authorised Person to recognise an on balance sheet Netting agreement, it must ensure a set of operational and legal conditions are satisfied: the asset and liability must be owing between the Authorised Person and the same Counterparty; netting must be performed consistently with the Authorised Person’s legal rights; a legal right of set off must exist; the agreement must not include a Walkaway Clause; and the netting must be effective and enforceable upon default, bankruptcy, liquidation, or similar circumstances affecting either party. The Authorised Person must also monitor, control, and manage the positions on a net basis and monitor and control roll off Exposure where there is a Maturity Mismatch. Finally, it must hold, for each relevant jurisdiction, a written and reasoned legal opinion from an appropriately qualified external legal adviser, confirming the key legal requirements and kept under review to remain current [#TGT:f3f3a9ac-35d6-4ee0-9390-c8543c3da4cf].",An Authorised Person may recognise as eligible the Netting of an on balance sheet Exposure against an offsetting on balance sheet item if the related Netting agreement meets the condition in Rule 4.13.19.,"On balance sheet Netting. For an Authorised Person to recognise an on balance sheet Netting agreement for the purposes of Rule 4.13.17, all of the following conditions must be satisfied:

column3: both the on balance sheet Exposure (asset) and the offsetting on balance sheet item (liability) are owing between the Authorised Person and the same Counterparty;

column2: the Authorised Person nets the on balance sheet Exposure (asset) and the offsetting on balance sheet item (liability) in a way that is consistent with its legal rights against the Counterparty;
a legal right of set off exists;
the agreement between the Authorised Person and the Counterparty does not contain a Walkaway Clause;

the Netting provided for in the agreement between the Authorised Person and the Counterparty is effective and enforceable in the event of default, bankruptcy, liquidation or other similar circumstances affecting either the Counterparty or the Authorised Person;
the on balance sheet Exposure (asset) and the offsetting on balance sheet item (liability) are monitored, controlled and managed on a net basis; and
the potential for roll off Exposure is monitored and controlled where there is a Maturity Mismatch; and
it has, in respect of each relevant jurisdiction, a written and reasoned legal opinion which:
has been provided by an external source of legal advice of appropriate professional standing;
confirms that the requirements of (1)(a) (e) are met for all relevant jurisdictions; and

is kept under review to ensure that it remains correct and up to date in the event of changes to the relevant laws.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,6446b9df-ac01-4d04-bb14-029e92f0b3f7,f3f3a9ac-35d6-4ee0-9390-c8543c3da4cf,,,4.13.17.(1),4.13.19,,,,,HV0093,cf8dd636cd9dd2cb,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,target_only_sufficient,

column1: deea83499d67e2c9,"A Mining Reporting Entity is expected to follow the non-mandatory parts of a Mining Reporting Standard. If its disclosure does not meet one of those non-mandatory requirements, what does it have to say in the disclosure?","The Regulator expects a Mining Reporting Entity to fully comply with all non-mandatory requirements set out in a Mining Reporting Standard, alongside the requirement to fully comply with all binding requirements in that Standard [#SRC:b8235755-7447-4ae5-b3dc-8cb14109c124]. If the Mining Reporting Entity’s disclosure nevertheless does not meet a non-mandatory requirement contained in the relevant Mining Reporting Standard, the entity must address that gap directly in the disclosure. Specifically, it must include a statement that explains (1) how the disclosure differs from the non-mandatory requirement and (2) why it differs, so the departure is clear and justified to the reader [#TGT:211edfe0-af57-41c8-84ca-814e1af3de0f]. In practice, this means the entity should not treat non-mandatory requirements as “ignore if inconvenient”; it should either comply fully with them as expected, or, where it does not, provide a transparent explanation within the disclosure itself describing the nature of the difference and the reasons for taking that approach.","Rule 11.2.1(1) requires a Mining Reporting Entity to fully comply with all binding requirements set out in a Mining Reporting Standard. The Regulator also expects a Mining Reporting Entity to fully comply with all non-mandatory requirements set out in a Mining Reporting Standard, including, for example, Table 1 of the JORC Code or SAMREC Code, or explain its non-compliance in accordance with Rule 11.2.2.","Requirements for all disclosures. Where a disclosure by a Mining Reporting Entity does not meet a non-mandatory requirement contained in a Mining Reporting Standard, the Mining Reporting Entity must provide in its disclosure a statement as to how and why its disclosure differs from the non-mandatory requirement contained in the relevant Mining Reporting Standard.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,b8235755-7447-4ae5-b3dc-8cb14109c124,211edfe0-af57-41c8-84ca-814e1af3de0f,,,11.2.2.Guidance,11.2.2,,,,,HV0094,deea83499d67e2c9,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

c354f4a6a30cbac7,"If an Authorised Person doing Virtual Asset regulated activities must follow the same capital approach as a Recognised Investment Exchange, what form must the Authorised Person’s regulatory capital be in, and how much capital does a Recognised Investment Exchange have to hold (including any extra buffer the Regulator can change)?","For an Authorised Person engaged in regulated activities in relation to Virtual Assets, the regulatory capital requirement is linked to the requirements that a Recognised Investment Exchange must meet, and the regulatory capital held by the Authorised Person must be in fiat form [#SRC:9795daec-7cae-4276-a676-296830fc723d]. Separately, a Recognised Investment Exchange has a clear obligation to hold capital based on its operational expenses: it shall hold an amount equal to 6 months’ operational expenses, and it shall also hold an additional buffer amount of up to a further 6 months’ operational expenses unless the Regulator directs otherwise [#TGT:1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96]. Putting these together, the Authorised Person must ensure its regulatory capital is held in the required form (fiat) while aligning its capital approach to the Recognised Investment Exchange standard, and the Recognised Investment Exchange must maintain both the baseline 6-month operational-expense capital and, unless changed by the Regulator, an additional buffer of up to another 6 months’ operational expenses [#SRC:9795daec-7cae-4276-a676-296830fc723d] [#TGT:1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96].","REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR AUTHORISED PERSONS ENGAGED IN REGULATED ACTIVITIES IN RELATION TO VIRTUAL ASSETS

Given the nature of, and the risks associated with Virtual Assets, COBS Rule 17.3 requires an Authorised Person to hold regulatory capital in a manner consistent with MIR Rule 3.2.1 (being the requirements that a Recognised Investment Exchange must meet). Pursuant to these Rules, regulatory capital held by an Authorised Person must be in fiat form.","A Recognised Investment Exchange shall hold the following capital:

column2: an amount equal to 6 months' operational expenses; plus

unless the Regulator directs otherwise, an additional buffer amount of up to a further 6 months' operational expenses.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,9795daec-7cae-4276-a676-296830fc723d,1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96,,,31),3.2.1,,,,,HV0095,c354f4a6a30cbac7,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: ab28308168b764d1,"If an RIE or MTF has to put in place arrangements that make sure parties’ rights and liabilities from trades on its platform are settled on time, when does engaging a Recognised Clearing House or a Remote Clearing House count as enough to meet that requirement, and what restriction is stated for Remote Clearing Houses in Digital Securities?","For an RIE or MTF, the core obligation is to have satisfactory arrangements that secure the timely discharge of the rights and liabilities of the parties to transactions taking place on its platform [#SRC:54798d14-a849-4384-81d3-79f14fca8fd4]. The paired definition explains how that obligation can be met in a streamlined way: if the RIE or MTF engages a Recognised Clearing House or a Remote Clearing House, that engagement is treated as sufficient to satisfy the requirement, i.e., it is deemed to meet the arrangements standard for timely discharge [#TGT:9217cc24-dbcc-43e5-8884-f398ee26b820]. At the same time, the source passage adds an important constraint for Digital Securities: it notes the FSRA’s position that it will not permit Remote Clearing Houses for this purpose in the Digital Securities context [#SRC:54798d14-a849-4384-81d3-79f14fca8fd4]. So, although the deemed-sufficient concept includes both types of clearing house in general terms [#TGT:9217cc24-dbcc-43e5-8884-f398ee26b820], an RIE or MTF dealing with Digital Securities should not plan to rely on a Remote Clearing House and should instead look to engagement of a Recognised Clearing House to satisfy the timely-discharge arrangements obligation [#SRC:54798d14-a849-4384-81d3-79f14fca8fd4].","DIGITAL SECURITIES SETTLEMENT

Pursuant to MIR Rule 3.8.1, RIEs or MTFs are required to have satisfactory arrangements for securing the timely discharge of the rights and liabilities of the parties to transactions taking place on its platform.   MIR Rule 3.8.2 normally allows for a RCH or Remote Clearing House (noting the FSRA’s position that it will not permit Remote Clearing Houses for this purpose in the context of Digital Securities) to be deemed as sufficient for the purposes of satisfying MIR Rule 3.8.1.",The engagement of a Recognised Clearing House or Remote Clearing House will be deemed sufficient to satisfy Rule 3.8.1.,SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,54798d14-a849-4384-81d3-79f14fca8fd4,9217cc24-dbcc-43e5-8884-f398ee26b820,,,56),3.8.2,,,,,HV0096,ab28308168b764d1,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

0bddd684a5a6da69,"When an Authorised Person is determining the credit risk weight to be used for Credit Risk Exposures based on credit assessments, what procedure must it follow to calculate risk-weighted assets for those exposures, and how does that procedure connect the exposure value to the credit risk weight used in the calculation?","Where credit assessments are used for the purpose of determining the credit risk weight for Credit Risk Exposures, the Authorised Person must apply the prescribed risk‑weighted assets calculation process for those Credit Risk Exposures [#SRC:dced9cf2-78fe-480a-9b65-4bff40564d27]. Specifically, to calculate its RWA for CR Exposures, it must first determine the Exposure value (E) for each on‑balance sheet and off‑balance sheet asset using the applicable exposure measurement methodology and recognising the effects of any applicable credit risk mitigation. It must then categorise each Exposure under the relevant rules, and allocate an applicable Credit Quality Grade and risk weight for that Exposure under the relevant rules. The Authorised Person must calculate the RWA amount for each CR Exposure using the formula RWA(CR) = E × CRW, where CRW is the applicable risk weight determined through the categorisation and credit quality grade/risk weight allocation steps. Finally, it must aggregate the results by adding the RWA amounts calculated for all of its CR Exposures to arrive at total RWA for CR Exposures [#TGT:5c99a9f9-b97d-4f45-834a-0562c13cf368].",This Section governs credit assessments of Exposures for the purpose of determining the CRW for Credit Risk (CR) Exposures as provided in Rule 4.8.3 and for securitisation (SE) Exposures as provided in Rule 4.8.4.,"Calculation of RWA for Credit Risk Exposures (CR Exposures). To calculate its RWA for CR Exposures, an Authorised Person must:

column2: calculate the value of the Exposure (represented as ""E"") for every on-balance sheet and every off balance sheet asset in accordance with the Exposure measurement methodology specified in Section 4.9 and recognising the effects of any applicable CRM;
categorise that Exposure in accordance with the Rules in Section 4.10;
allocate an applicable Credit Quality Grade and risk weight for that Exposure in accordance with the Rules in Section 4.11 and 4.12;
calculate the RWA amount for that Exposure using the following formula: RWA(CR) = E x CRW
RWA(CR)"" refers to the risk weighted Exposure amount for that CR Exposure;
E"" refers to the Exposure value or amount, for that CR Exposure; and
CRW"" refers to the applicable risk weight for that CR Exposure determined in accordance with (b) and (c); and

add the RWA amounts calculated in accordance with (d) for all its CR Exposures.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,dced9cf2-78fe-480a-9b65-4bff40564d27,5c99a9f9-b97d-4f45-834a-0562c13cf368,,,4.11.Guidance,4.8.3,,,,,HV0097,0bddd684a5a6da69,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,target_only_sufficient,

column1: bb24724bb265896b,"When an Authorised Person engaged in regulated activities in relation to Virtual Assets aligns its regulatory capital approach to the requirements that apply to a Recognised Investment Exchange, what form must that regulatory capital take, and what minimum capital amounts must a Recognised Investment Exchange hold (including any buffer that may be varied by the Regulator)?","An Authorised Person engaged in regulated activities in relation to Virtual Assets must hold its regulatory capital in a manner consistent with the requirements that a Recognised Investment Exchange must meet, and—under those requirements—the regulatory capital held by the Authorised Person must be in fiat form [#SRC:9795daec-7cae-4276-a676-296830fc723d]. In parallel, the Recognised Investment Exchange is subject to a specific capital holding obligation: it shall hold capital equal to 6 months’ operational expenses, and it shall also hold an additional buffer amount of up to a further 6 months’ operational expenses unless the Regulator directs otherwise [#TGT:1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96]. Read together, the framework ties the Authorised Person’s regulatory capital approach to the Recognised Investment Exchange capital standard while also imposing a distinct form requirement on the Authorised Person (fiat), and it defines the Recognised Investment Exchange’s baseline and potential buffer capital amounts, with the buffer subject to direction by the Regulator [#SRC:9795daec-7cae-4276-a676-296830fc723d] [#TGT:1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96].","REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR AUTHORISED PERSONS ENGAGED IN REGULATED ACTIVITIES IN RELATION TO VIRTUAL ASSETS

Given the nature of, and the risks associated with Virtual Assets, COBS Rule 17.3 requires an Authorised Person to hold regulatory capital in a manner consistent with MIR Rule 3.2.1 (being the requirements that a Recognised Investment Exchange must meet). Pursuant to these Rules, regulatory capital held by an Authorised Person must be in fiat form.","A Recognised Investment Exchange shall hold the following capital:

column2: an amount equal to 6 months' operational expenses; plus

unless the Regulator directs otherwise, an additional buffer amount of up to a further 6 months' operational expenses.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,9795daec-7cae-4276-a676-296830fc723d,1f2f00c6-1680-4516-adc8-b360f33ebe96,,,31),3.2.1,,,,,HV0098,bb24724bb265896b,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 893586bb931cb773,"If the Regulator thinks a Listed Entity being admitted to the Official List needs quarterly cash reports (for example, because it is admitted under the assets eligibility test, has less than three years of audited financial statements, or is a cash-box), what does the Reporting Entity have to do each quarter when the Regulator also requires quarterly reporting as a condition of admission or because it classifies the Reporting Entity as a Mining Exploration Reporting Entity or a Petroleum Exploration Reporting Entity?","If the Regulator generally expects quarterly cash reporting because the Listed Entity being admitted to the Official List is admitted under the assets eligibility test, has less than three years of audited financial statements, or is otherwise considered to need quarterly cash reports (including where the admission is of a cash-box), that sets the circumstances in which the Regulator may impose a quarterly reporting requirement on the Reporting Entity [#SRC:ef54c7e6-d860-4e8b-aed8-ddcd2cbacab8]. When the Regulator then actually triggers that requirement—by making it a condition of admission to the Official List, by classifying the Reporting Entity as a Mining Exploration Reporting Entity or a Petroleum Exploration Reporting Entity, or by otherwise requiring quarterly reporting—the Reporting Entity must complete MKT Form 10-1 on a quarterly basis [#TGT:67e6fb61-6313-4d10-b3bb-b9b99d81cb75]. In other words, the “quarterly cash reports” expectation described in the circumstances above is met, when required by the Regulator, through the concrete action of completing MKT Form 10-1 every quarter. The key is that the quarterly obligation applies only when the Regulator requires it in one of the specified ways, and then it must be done quarterly.","The Regulator will generally require a Reporting Entity to comply with Rule 10.1.3B(1)(i) in circumstances where the Listed Entity with Securities being admitted to the Official List is admitted under the assets eligibility test (see Rule 2.3.16), has less than three years of audited financial statements as prescribed in Rule 2.3.2(1), or is considered by the Regulator, for other reasons, to require quarterly cash reports, such as the admission of a cash-box.","A Reporting Entity must complete MKT Form 10-1 on a quarterly basis if the Regulator:

column2: requires it as a condition of admission to the Official List pursuant to section 52(1)(b) of the FSMR;
classifies the Reporting Entity as a Mining Exploration Reporting Entity or a Petroleum Exploration Reporting Entity; or

requires it pursuant to section 84 of the FSMR.",SCHEMA,,basic,ADGM,hard_enriched,ef54c7e6-d860-4e8b-aed8-ddcd2cbacab8,67e6fb61-6313-4d10-b3bb-b9b99d81cb75,,,10.1.3B.(1).Guidance.1.,10.1.3B.(1),,,,,HV0099,893586bb931cb773,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,

column1: 57dadba191a2b41c,"When Securities are Exempt Securities and are being admitted to trading on a Recognised Investment Exchange, is a person still prohibited from having those Securities admitted unless there is an Approved Prospectus, or does the prohibition not apply (subject to any stated requirement)?","A person is generally prohibited from having Securities admitted to trading on a Recognised Investment Exchange unless there is an Approved Prospectus in relation to the relevant Securities [#TGT:82ade9b4-bba4-449c-815c-32d6ef292b54]. However, where the admission to trading on a Recognised Investment Exchange concerns Securities that are Exempt Securities, the stated prohibition does not apply, provided the admission is subject to the specified requirement referenced for that exemption framework [#SRC:f70272ac-30bf-4e62-92d7-8b863f75cdf9]. In practical compliance terms, this means you must first determine whether the Securities qualify as Exempt Securities for the purpose of admission to trading, and then ensure the admission is conducted in accordance with the applicable requirement tied to that exemption. If the Securities are not Exempt Securities (or the relevant requirement is not met), the default position remains that the person must not proceed with admission to trading on the Recognised Investment Exchange without an Approved Prospectus for the relevant Securities [#TGT:82ade9b4-bba4-449c-815c-32d6ef292b54].","The prohibition in section 61(1) of the FSMR does not apply, subject to the requirement in Rule 4.4.2, to the admission to trading on a Recognised Investment Exchange of Securities that are Exempt Securities under Rule 4.4.1.","A person shall not, subject to subsection ‎(3)—

column2: make an Offer of Securities in the Abu Dhabi Global Market; or
have Securities admitted to trading on a Recognised Investment Exchange;

column1: unless there is an Approved Prospectus in relation to the relevant Securities.",SCHEMA,,professional,ADGM,hard_enriched,f70272ac-30bf-4e62-92d7-8b863f75cdf9,82ade9b4-bba4-449c-815c-32d6ef292b54,,,4.4.Guidance.2.,Part 6.Chapter 1.61.(1),,,,,HV0100,57dadba191a2b41c,ObliQA-XRef_Out_Datasets/final_large_merged/ObliQA-XRef-ADGM-ALL/final.jsonl,yes,mostly_natural_rephrased,both_needed,
